title: [Exclusive/Nanyang Rich List] Lim Kok Thay has fallen out of the top ten, and Technology tycoons are all in decline.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Exclusive Report:@Jungle lee
Initially, 2024 was expected to be a bountiful year of "Dragon Roaring in the Sky," but reality turned out to be contrary. Gambling and Technology stocks became the biggest losers, with stock prices continuously falling, and there is almost no hope of a rebound.
Notably, the head of Malaysian gambling giant Genting (GENTING, 3182, Main Board Consumer Stocks), Tan Sri Lim Guohai, who has long held a place in the top ten of the Nanyang Rich List, saw a significant reduction in wealth in 2024, unexpectedly falling out of the top ten rankings, shocking the market.
Will 2025 bring a turning point of "Snake All Beautiful"? Finding a way to stage a spectacular comeback has become a common expectation of the market and investors.
Follow the footsteps of the 'Nanyang Siang Pau' to uncover the rise and fall of Gambling and Technology Stocks in the '2024 Nanyang Rich List'.
The stock prices of Genting siblings have plummeted.
Lim Kuo Tai's wealth evaporated by 16%.
In 2024, Malaysia's Gambling Industry faces a difficult moment, Genting. $GENTING (3182.MY)$ and Genting Malaysia. $GENM (4715.MY)$ are undoubtedly at the eye of the storm, unable to extricate themselves.
The sharp decline in stock prices and shrinking Market Cap not only caused the Genting siblings to fall out of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Composite Index constituent stocks list, but also directly affected the personal wealth of the group's helm, Genting Chairman and CEO Tan Sri Lim Kuo Tai.
As of the end of December, Genting Group's Market Cap has fallen to 15 billion Ringgit, ranking 34th in the Malaysian stock market, while Genting Malaysia stands at 13.4 billion Ringgit, ranking 37th.
This dismal performance has caused the share prices of the Genting duo to plummet from their peak, especially for Genting Malaysia, whose stock price has dropped from 6 Ringgit in 2017 to 2.26 Ringgit by the end of 2024.
Lim Kok Thay's wealth has also evaporated by nearly 16%, making him one of the personalities with the most severe decline in the 2024 Nanyang Rich List.
The accumulation of multiple adverse factors is the main reason that has led the Genting duo into trouble.
From the dispute regarding the 20th Century Fox theme park in 2018, to the gambling tax increase in 2019, and the severe impact of the pandemic on the tourism industry in 2020, Genting Group's profitability has been long constrained.
Additionally, the recent intensification of global economic uncertainty and tightening liquidity in the Capital Markets have caused investors to lose confidence in the Gambling industry.
$Genting Sing (G13.SG)$
The overall Gambling industry remains sluggish.
In 2024, while Genting World's gambling revenue has returned to 90% of the 2019 level, the overall performance of the industry is still sluggish, with market sentiment deeply affected by the adjustments of component stocks.
Analysts point out that the valuation of the Genting Twins has dropped to a historical low, which is 1.5 to 2 standard deviations below the average.
However, ongoing negative news and uncertainty keep investors cautious.
To make matters worse, Genting Malaysia is being sued by its partner at RW Bimini in the Bahamas for alleged accounting fraud, seeking $0.6 billion (approximately 2.575 billion Ringgit) in damages.
The company's wholly-owned U.S. subsidiary, Genting Americas (GAI), was sued by RAV Bahamas Ltd. (RAV) on October 7, 2024, local time, in the Federal District Court for the Southern District of Florida, with the lawsuit notification served to GAI on October 11.
The statement mentions that the lawsuit involves operational matters related to RW Bimini, with RAV claiming over $0.6 billion in damages.
Worse still, Genting Sing's predicament worsens, as analysts downgrade its stock rating due to poor earnings, causing the stock price to drop to a two-year low.
Is rebirth in adversity the way back to glory?
In the face of adversity, Lim Kook Thai and the management team are seeking breakthroughs, looking towards 2025, planning to diversify their business and gradually revive their core Gambling business to restore market confidence, with the return of international tourists and growth in domestic consumption likely to be key drivers.
Analysts predict that the Gambling Industry will fully rebound in profitability by the first half of 2025, with Genting Malaysia's gambling revenue expected to return to 2019 levels.
In addition, the progress of Genting Malaysia's application for a full casino license in New York, USA, is also attracting attention, as success in this endeavor would add 0.47 billion Ringgit to the group's annual EBITDA, greatly enhancing profitability.
Meanwhile, the UK pharmaceutical company TauRx, in which Genting holds a 20.33% stake, is seen as a major potential growth point.
Its Alzheimer’s drug - HMTM, is currently advancing through the approval and commercialization process, and TauRx has a potential valuation of up to 15 billion USD, which, if progress goes smoothly, could bring a potential value of 3.54 Ringgit per share to Genting.
As for its subsidiary, Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV), to restore the company's reputation, a new board of directors was announced at the end of December last year to shake off the stigma of alleged involvement in money laundering activities.
Will things go as smoothly as expected?
Of course, the road to recovery will not be as smooth as anticipated, as there are uncertainties regarding the New York state casino license, the protracted cycle of TauRx's commercialization, and potential fluctuations in the overall economic environment, all of which are challenges that need to be overcome.
Analysts warn that despite the attractive high dividend yields and low valuations of Genting's dual entities, the likelihood of a significant rebound in stock prices in the short term is low.
Lin Guotai and Genting Group's ability to reverse the situation by 2025 will become a focus of market attention.
After gradually digesting the negative factors, the Genting duo may welcome a moderate recovery. However, whether they can survive and make breakthroughs in adversity will depend on the effectiveness of their Business diversification strategy and the recovery speed of their core Gambling business.
US technology stocks continue to hit record highs.
The new Malaysian tech giants are facing a decline.
While US technology stocks set new highs in 2024, the Malaysian Technology Sector is mired in difficulties, with continuously poor stock performance, disappointing the market.
This phenomenon breaks the historical trend of a high positive correlation between global Semiconductors sales and the Malaysian Technology Sector, showing a reverse relationship.
What are the reasons behind this change? Looking ahead to 2025, can the Malaysian Technology field welcome dawn? Will Trump's return have potential impacts?
Looking at the '2024 Nanyang Rich List', it is not difficult to see that the tycoons involved in the Technology Sector are all facing a significant wealth depletion issue.
Among them, the helm of Meijia First. $MFCB (3069.MY)$ And the Emperor and Hong. $D&O (7204.MY)$ Wu Nanhua and his family experienced a decline in wealth of 0.5 billion Ringgit or 17%, falling from 23rd place in 2023 to 32nd place.
Although Meijia First is involved in a large number of renewable Energy Assets and has successfully climbed the Datacenter train, its stock price rose 24% for the year, however, Emperor and Hong had no such luck, with a stock price trend opposite to Meijia First, plummeting 42%.
This drop is enough to pull down Wu Nanhua and his family's wealth ranking by 9 positions.
Additionally, other technology tycoons facing declines in wealth include UWC company. $UWC (5292.MY)$ Executive Director and Group CEO Dato' Huang Cairong and Liu Jiqiang, whose billionaire ranking fell from 27th to 36th, with a wealth decline of 0.26 billion Ringgit or 10.1%, coming to 2.31 billion Ringgit.
As for Ge Dai Technology. $GREATEC (0208.MY)$ The overall CEO, Datuk Chen Rongqi, also performed poorly, with his ranking dropping from 20th to 27th, and his wealth decreased by 0.34 billion Ringgit, or 9.2%, to 3.37 billion Ringgit.
Trump becomes a new variable.
In fact, the external market is filled with many uncertainties, and Trump's policies may once again affect the performance of Global technology stocks.
Potential bullish opportunities include Trump's possible continuation of his 'America First' policy, which could drive investment and growth in USA businesses, thus boosting the technology sector in USA stocks. Some Malaysian technology companies, as part of the Global supply chain, may have the opportunity to benefit indirectly from the expansion of demand in the USA market.
The potential risk is that Trump may restart the tariff policies on products from China or strengthen protectionism in the technology sector, thus intensifying the technology competition between China and USA, disrupting the Global supply chain, and putting pressure on Malaysian technology stocks that are highly dependent on international markets.
Of course, the slowdown in Global auto sales and the frequent release of weak earnings reports by European luxury car brands have made investors adopt a more cautious attitude towards companies related to automotive technology semiconductors.
In Malaysia's Technology Sector, companies such as DNB and Tenda Technology, $PENTA (7160.MY)$ The Pacific, $MPI (3867.MY)$ and others have recently seen their performance impacted.
In contrast, there are very few companies benefiting from the AI sector. $FRONTKN (0128.MY)$ Among them, Frontline Technology has performed the best, with its client Taiwan Semiconductor directly benefiting from NVIDIA's continued strength.
Taiwan Semiconductor's latest performance shows a net profit growth of 57% year-on-year, and it is expected that revenue will further increase by 25% in 2025.
With the halo effect of AI, Frontline Technology's stock price broke the historical high of 4.78 Ringgit in July 2024. Although future performance looks bullish, the risk of overvaluation should not be ignored, and investors need to remain cautious in their planning.
The recovery is still full of uncertainty.
Despite the Malaysian Technology Index declining for two consecutive years, it edged up 2.5% to 64.89 points by the end of 2024, but started poorly in 2025, dropping nearly 6%.
US economic data exceeded expectations, and the Federal Reserve's potential pause on interest rate cuts or even a return to rate hikes further pressured the performance of overvalued companies.
Additionally, the recovery path for Malaysian Technology companies is not smooth.
Packaging and testing companies such as Inari Amertron $INARI (0166.MY)$ , Mat Pacific $MPI (3867.MY)$ , Unison $UNISEM (5005.MY)$ have all seen their stock prices drop to a one-year low this year, reflecting market's short-term lack of confidence in this sector.
Facing uncertainties in outside markets and the complex environment with "madman Trump" returning to politics, investors may need to shift their focus rather than concentrate on individual sectors.
The limitation of the Technology Sector in Malaysia is that the majority of companies are concentrated in the mid to downstream fields, such as backend packaging testing and electronic assembly, lacking upstream chip design capabilities.
NVIDIA holds a dominant position.
Although AI has driven Global semiconductor sales, this growth is mainly concentrated in the USA market, with NVIDIA contributing a significant proportion.
It is worth mentioning that global semiconductor sales are expected to grow by 12.5% in 2025, reaching 687 billion USD (approximately 3.1 trillion Ringgit), but when excluding NVIDIA's revenue, Global semiconductor sales are actually stagnant.
This further highlights the importance of top companies and the structural opportunities in the field of AI.
Looking back at Malaysia, most tech companies are still focused on the fields of communication, Smart Phones, Autos, and industrial sectors.
However, the slowdown in Smart Phone shipment growth, along with massive layoffs in the automotive sector, all reflect weak demand for end products, and coupled with the aggressive interest rate hikes by various central banks, exert pressure on the recovery of profits in the Malaysian Technology Sector.
Overall, although the Technology Sector in Malaysia is still struggling in a quagmire, the rebound signals from some companies may bring new hope to investors, and these companies need to focus more precisely on quality growth to capitalize on the high-end Technology fields.

title: Genting collaborates with SDIC Power Holdings to construct the second phase of the Photovoltaic Power Station in Fujian.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, October 20) Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ The wholly-owned subsidiary Genting MZW has signed a cooperation framework agreement with SDIC Power Holdings to jointly develop the second phase project of a 100-megawatt aquaculture complementary Photovoltaic Power Station in Dongwu Cha A District, Putian City, Fujian.
According to the announcement, the two parties have previously collaborated to promote the first phase project of the power station (100 megawatts), which is expected to commence in September 2024 and start operation in May 2025. Based on the success of the first phase, both parties have decided to initiate the second phase construction.
The second phase project will be adjacent to the first phase and share the substation, adopting a model that combines aquaculture with solar energy generation, setting up photovoltaic panels on the water surface to achieve synchronized development of clean energy production and eco-friendly aquaculture.
The project is planned to commence in July 2025 and is expected to be completed in 2026, which will add 100 megawatts of clean energy capacity, with an estimated annual power generation of 0.274 billion kilowatt-hours, aiding Fujian Province's renewable energy development goals and supporting China's 'dual carbon' strategy.
Genting Group holds a 39% stake in both the first and second phase projects, while SDIC Power Holdings holds a 61% stake.
The chairman and CEO of Genting, Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay, stated that the project not only demonstrates the group's expansion in the renewable energy sector but also further strengthens the long-term cooperation relationship with SDIC Power Holdings established for over 20 years.
The two sides have also jointly developed several large power projects in China and Indonesia, including the Zhoushan 2×745 megawatt H-class hydrogen gas plant and the 660-megawatt plant in Banten, Indonesia.
Lin Guotai emphasized that both parties will continue to deepen cooperation in the future, exploring more opportunities for clean Energy development and contributing to Global Energy innovation and sustainable development.

title: Genting Financial Report 27/2/2025
author: 不吃鱼
body:
I. Financial Condition Analysis
1. Revenue and Profit Performance
– Q4 2024: Revenue was 6.881 billion ringgit, a decrease of 5.3% year-on-year, indicating short-term business pressure; gross profit was 1.893 billion ringgit, down 15.4% year-on-year, reflecting challenges in cost control or gross margin compression; pre-tax profit was 0.238 billion ringgit, a significant decline of 72.5% year-on-year, with a net loss attributable to shareholders of 0.169 billion ringgit (profit of 0.15 billion ringgit in the same period last year), indicating a significant deterioration in profitability in the fourth quarter.
– Annual Performance: Revenue was 27.717 billion ringgit, a year-on-year growth of 2.2%, with slight growth maintained throughout the year; gross profit was 8.099 billion ringgit, down 5.3% year-on-year; pre-tax profit was 3.3 billion ringgit, down 7.5% year-on-year; net income attributable to shareholders was 0.883 billion ringgit, a decrease of 5.0% year-on-year. Although annual profit has declined, it still remains positive overall.
AnalysisThe losses in the fourth quarter may be due to seasonal factors (such as off-peak tourism) or one-time costs (such as legal litigation fees or asset impairment), while overall positive growth throughout the year indicates that the company still has considerable resilience. However, the narrowing profit margin and losses in the fourth quarter should be taken seriously, as they may signal fluctuations in profitability in the short term.
2. Balance Sheet
– Total Assets: As of December 31, 2024, total assets were 105.093 billion ringgit, a decrease of 1.6% compared to 106.834 billion ringgit in 2023, indicating a slight contraction in asset size.
– Total Liabilities: 51.602 billion ringgit, an increase of 1.8% compared to 50.703 billion ringgit in 2023, indicating a slight rise in debt levels.
– Shareholder Equity: 32.253 billion ringgit, a year-on-year decrease of 4.2%. The reduction in net assets may relate to dividend distributions or comprehensive income losses caused by Forex fluctuations.
– Leverage Ratio: The debt/assets ratio is approximately 49%, slightly increased from 47.5% in 2023. Financial leverage is within a controllable range, but attention should be given to the risk of rising debt costs.
3. Cash Flow
– Operating Cash Flow: 7.123 billion ringgit, a year-on-year decrease of 5.3%, showing a weakened cash generation capacity in core business.
– Investing Cash Flow: Net outflow of 4.064 billion ringgit, significantly increased from 1.357 billion ringgit in 2023, reflecting the company's high capital expenditure on infrastructure upgrades and new projects.
– Financing Cash Flow: Net outflow of 3.699 billion ringgit, a decrease compared to 6.006 billion ringgit in 2023, indicating that the pressure of debt repayment has eased.
AnalysisDue to a decline in operational cash flow coupled with high investment expenditures, cash reserves decreased from 23.66 billion ringgit in 2023 to 22.404 billion ringgit. Nevertheless, the company still has sufficient liquidity buffer (approximately 21% of total Assets), ensuring short-term debt repayment capacity. However, if investment returns do not meet expectations, financial pressure may increase.
II. Business Performance Analysis
Genting Group's business is diversified, covering five major Sectors: Leisure & Hospitality, Plantation, Electrical Utilities, Real Estate, and Oil & Gas. The following analysis is provided for each sector:
1. Leisure & Hospitality Sector (82.9% revenue share)
– Revenue: 22.986 billion ringgit, accounting for 82.9% of total revenue, still the absolute core.
– Adjusted EBITDA: 5.903 billion ringgit, a 7.9% year-on-year decline, affected by seasonality, Exchange Rates fluctuations, and market competition.
– Regional Performance: Malaysia (Genting World), Singapore (Resorts World Sentosa), United Kingdom, and USA markets showed varied performance, with a significant impact from the off-season in the fourth quarter.
AnalysisThis sector is the profit pillar of the group, but performance in 2024 is expected to be weak, possibly related to the uneven global recovery in tourism and rising costs. Plans to launch new attractions and promotional activities (such as the 60th anniversary celebration) in 2025 are expected to boost revenue.
2. Plantation
– Revenue: 3.258 billion Ringgit, a year-on-year increase of 10.2%.
– Adjusted EBITDA: 0.868 billion Ringgit, a year-on-year increase of 17.6%, benefiting from rising palm oil prices and increased production.
AnalysisThe plantation performed strongly and became a highlight for 2024. Palm oil prices are expected to remain stable in the short term, and new planting areas in Indonesia will enhance production, making 2025's performance promising.
3. Electrical Utilities
– Revenue: 1.216 billion Ringgit, an increase of 8.6% year-on-year.
– Adjusted EBITDA: 0.341 billion Ringgit, an increase of 12.5% year-on-year, driven by demand growth in Indonesia and China.
AnalysisThe Electrical Utilities sector shows steady growth, the rising demand for electrical utilities in Asia provides long-term bullish potential, but attention is needed on the potential impact of the transition to wind power on traditional business.
4. Real Estate
– Revenue: 0.465 billion Ringgit, a decrease of 5.5% year-on-year.
– Adjusted EBITDA: 0.141 billion Ringgit, a decrease of 11.3% year-on-year, affected by market competition and rising costs.
AnalysisThe Real Estate sector is performing poorly, but the opening of new projects in Indonesia in 2025 (such as Jakarta Premium Outlets) may bring a turnaround, requiring attention to market acceptance.
5. Oil & Gas
– Revenue: 0.375 billion ringgit, a year-on-year decrease of 14.8%.
– Adjusted EBITDA: 0.282 billion ringgit, a year-on-year decrease of 19.4%, affected by global oil price fluctuations and reduced output.
AnalysisThe Oil & Gas Business is significantly affected by external factors; the performance of the China project may improve in 2025, but geopolitical risks remain uncertain.
III. Industry Trend Analysis
1. Leisure and Hospitality: The global tourism industry continues to recover, with growth expected in the Malaysia, Singapore, and USA markets, but geopolitical and economic uncertainties may suppress demand.
2. Plantation: Palm oil prices are expected to stabilize by 2025, but increasing competition may压低 profit margins.
3. Electrical Utilities: The growth in power demand in Asia is Bullish, and the trend of Wind Power needs attention.
4. Real Estate: There is growth potential in the markets of Malaysia and Indonesia, but competition is fierce.
5. Oil & Gas: Crude Oil Product prices are highly volatile, and geopolitical risks are significant.
AnalysisThe group's diversified Business allows it to mitigate risks in a single Industry, but the core Leisure and Hotel Operations are highly sensitive to macroeconomic conditions and travel trends, requiring close monitoring of the Global economic recovery pace.
Four, Risk Factor Analysis
1. Exchange Rate Risk: Business operations across multiple countries are susceptible to fluctuation in Exchange Rates, and Forex losses have already emerged in the fourth quarter of 2024.
2. Geopolitical risks: The tourism industry and Oil & Gas business are vulnerable to the impacts of global conflicts.
3. Market competition: Leisure and hospitality, Real Estate, and plantations face intense competition.
4. Legal risks: Lawsuits in the USA and Bahamas may bring financial and reputational pressures (e.g. RAV Bahamas vs Genting Americas, with claims exceeding 0.6 billion USD).
5. Operational risks: Natural disasters or equipment failures can disrupt business operations.
AnalysisLegal and Exchange Rates risks are the most urgent in the short term; if the lawsuit outcomes are unfavorable, it may lead to increased cash flow pressures.
Five, future development strategy and outlook.
1. Strategy direction.
– Leisure and Hotels: Invest in infrastructure and new attractions (such as Singapore RWS 2.0), optimize operational efficiency.
– Plantations: Improve yield and quality, develop new projects.
– Electrical Utilities: Develop Wind Power, enhance efficiency.
– Real Estate: Launch new projects (such as the Indonesia project), increase market share.
– Oil & Gas: Increase production, advance new projects (such as the Kasuri block FLNG facility).
2. Outlook for 2025.
– Bullish factors:
◦ The tourism industry continues to recover, RWS 1.5 and the 60th anniversary event are expected to boost revenue.
The plantation benefits from the increase in palm oil prices and production.
Electrical Utilities and Oil & Gas projects (China, Indonesia) gradually release value.
– Challenges:
The loss in the fourth quarter may extend into the off-season.
Legal lawsuits and fluctuations in Exchange Rates may erode profits.
High capital expenditures (4.064 billion ringgit) need to match the returns.
PredictionRevenue is expected to grow moderately (5%-8%) by 2025, and the performance of core Leisure and hotel sectors will be key. If the Global economy stabilizes and new projects proceed as planned, EBITDA is expected to recover to the range of 6 billion-6.5 billion ringgit. However, if lawsuits or macro risks worsen, Net income may be pressured to 0.5 billion-0.7 billion ringgit.
Six, Recommendations
1. Risk Management: Enhance Forex hedging and legal responses to reduce uncertainty.
2. Business Optimization: Divest low-efficiency Assets (such as some Real Estate) and focus resources on high-return Sectors.
3. Innovative Investment: Accelerate AI and Wind Power deployment to enhance long-term competitiveness.
4. Brand Building: Strengthen marketing efforts to consolidate regional market positions.
5. Financial Strategy: Control debt costs and optimize capital structure.
Conclusion.
Genting Group faces challenges from a soft Leisure and hotel industry and fourth-quarter losses in 2024, but the stable performance of the plantation and Electrical Utilities Sectors provides support. In the future, the company is expected to achieve recovery through diversified strategies and focused investments, although external risks must be monitored.

author: 风起云涌LBF
body:
In normal circumstances, stock friends with limited funds will choose one of two. The simple theory is that based on past dividend records, buying the relatively cheaper GENM (2.xx) with the same capital will yield a higher dividend return compared to buying GENTING (4.xx) (both have almost the same dividend (0.15 per year), hence buying GENM yields more).

The second point is at what price you bought each stock, what your current average holding price is, and how many shares you have (the key point is if both stocks continue to decline now, should you withdraw part of your funds to keep or are you capable of entering at the next low point to lower your average holding price).

No one makes a huge profit right after buying (except through luck). It is common to encounter declines after buying (it could be a sudden storm drop or an asymmetrical error in assessment). The focus is on how to appropriately handle it when it occurs based on your own abilities and adjust your strategy.

My average holding price for GENM is 2.53 and the number of shares is not large (originally planned budget knowing that if it cannot maintain its position in the 30 major KLCI stocks, the share price will continue to drop. So originally prepared funds to buy at low prices in a 1-to-1 ratio, initially having 10 lots x 1,000 shares. Today, I have already bought another 10 lots x 1,000 shares).
GENM has a 25-year verified principle, the 2328 principle, which suggests that buying is suitable when below 2.3 and selling is suitable when above 2.8. My current average price is below 2.3, waiting for the dividend ex-date (there are two buying points for reference: one is 2.06 (its latest low point), and one is 1.86 (the low point during MCO)).

Kazuma Junro.

title: Poor performance has faced selling pressure, and the Market Cap of the Genting duo has evaporated by over 3.3 billion.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
The quarterly performance turned red, and the key figure, Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay, has left the management team. $GENTING (3182.MY)$ Genting and $GENM (4715.MY)$ Genting Malaysia's stock price suffered a double blow today, with the Market Cap of the duo evaporating by more than 3.3 billion Ringgit overnight!
Genting (GENTING) saw a drop of nearly 12%, while Genting Malaysia (GENM) experienced a more severe decline, plunging by as much as 16%.
Due to adverse Forex conditions and the weakening of Leisure and Entertainment business, Genting and Genting Malaysia both turned from profit to loss by the end of the 2024 fiscal year (as of December), with net losses of 0.1 billion Ringgit and 0.4 billion Ringgit respectively.
At the same time, Genting also announced several personnel changes, including Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay stepping down as CEO after nearly 20 years in the position to become Executive Chairman.
Meanwhile, President, COO, and Executive Director Dato' Sri Chen Guanghan will assume the role of CEO, effective from March 1.
Chen Guanghan will also step down from the position of CEO of Genting Plantations. $GENP (2291.MY)$ The CEO position will be taken over by the current Deputy CEO Dato' Indra Lin Konghui, also effective from March 1.
Lin Gonghui is the eldest son of Lin Guotai.

title: For 19 consecutive weeks, there has been a major outflow as foreign investors aggressively sold Malaysian stocks last week, totaling 1.27 billion.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 3rd) Foreign funds continued to sell Malaysian stocks last week, with an even heavier selling intensity, recording a net sell of 1.2 billion 70 million Ringgit for the week, maintaining the net selling trend for the 19th week.
MIDF Research pointed out through the Capital Trend report that foreign funds continuously fled Malaysian stocks last week, with the heaviest selling occurring on Friday, recording a net sell of 0.6 billion 46.2 million Ringgit.
The three major sectors that saw foreign outflow last week were financial services (-0.3 billion 62.1 million Ringgit), consumer and services (-0.3 billion 14.9 million Ringgit), and utilities (-0.2 billion 55.1 million Ringgit).
In contrast, the sectors with the most foreign purchases were construction (24.1 million Ringgit), telecommunications and media (14.7 million Ringgit), and REITs (6.7 million Ringgit).
In comparison, local Institutions remained the backbone of Malaysian stocks, with a net buy of 0.8 billion 17.4 million Ringgit.
Retail investors continued to enter last week, with a total net buy of 0.4 billion 47.9 million Ringgit of Malaysian stocks.
In terms of participation, the average daily trading volume (ADTV) fluctuated significantly last week, with foreign capital increasing by 80.3%, local Institutions rising by 5.8%; retail investors declined by 1.6%.

title: Bursa Q4 Earnings Summary And Reflection
author: Ultraboom
body:
Bursa just wrapped up its earnings season, >1000 companies have reported their earnings, and this might be the worst QR season I've experienced since I started investing in 2023, many companies experienced >10% with some even >30% dump since start of 2025. Those that reported good earnings didnt even see any bump, but rather get to keep their current price level. Bursa is currrently in a bear market, defensive picks tend to do well, as we can see below
Winners :
1. Plantation : I would say the biggest winners this season is plantation, most reported record QR, some even on track for record year, most paid dividend, some even special dividends. But most didnt see any share price rally, but in a bear market where everything is crashing, not getting dumped is a good thing, with a nice dividend as a reward for holding. Moving forward, as long as CPO price can maintain at current level, baring any external factors, i expect them to do well for the rest of 2025. (PS - my current largest holding is a plantation stock).
2. Banks : This is no surprise as banks tend to do well as long as country economy is doing well, msia GDP growth for Q4 2024 was 5%, down from 5.4% in Q3 but full year gdp growth was 5.1% which is much improved from 3.6% in 2023. Lesson for retailers reading this, banks are proxy to a countries economy, most malaysian banks are conventional banks aka 'farmers', they tend to do so so, tracking gdp growth of a country, this contrast investment banks or IBs, which is more 'hunter' business, their performance tend to track stock market performance. I tend to avoid investing in msian banks cos I'm looking for higher returns, and i dont see banks delivering 15-20% yoy growth on earnings, but i did have a good call on $ABMB (2488.MY)$ in 2023, the thesis was they are the bank with the highest ROE while having lowest PBV, and their value was realised when All eyes on Vertical Theme’s next move in Alliance Bank
3. Reits : Same as banks, reits tend to do so so, as property is a stable business, im also not a fan of reits, for the same reason as banks, the return isnt high enough to justify the effort and risk im taking. I did owned $PAVREIT (5212.MY)$ in 2023 when i started investing, it was a good call as at that time market 'forgot' that they injected pavillion bukit jalil into the trust but the value wasnt reflected back then
Losers
1. Technology : By far the biggest loser is technology, esp OSAT and ATE players, with only a few exceptions like $FRONTKN (0128.MY)$ maybe $KGB (0151.MY)$ if u consider KGB as a 'semicon' counter, the other OSAT and ATE players are facing double whammy of reducing sales and compressed margins, mainly from competition from china players, which are competing for both orders and at a cheaper price, this is a very grim outlook. On top of all that, the OSAT players need to spend capex on advance packaging as not to be left behind. Decreasing revenue, compressed margins and need for more capex, i personally do not have any ATE or OSAT counters as i view them as almost the start of sunset industry, similar to what happened to gloves after covid. The only way out for them is to spend capex to upgrade themselves, but whether they can spend capex to catch up before they run out of money is the big question, the only promising one is $VITROX (0097.MY)$ hence they got to keep their relatively higher valuation vs peers, but do they deserve that high valuation given they are going to spend capex and will face compressed margins? only time will tell. I'm glad that i cut loss on $TTVHB (0272.MY)$ earlier, as the stock is down another 50% from my exit price, guess my call was right.
2. Oil And Gas : Another badly hit sector, most O&G counters in bursa are petronas capex contractors, hence relying on petronas contracts, their performance tend to track petronas capex cycle, given petronas recent 'rightsizing'(should just call it downsizing), the sentiment has been poor, even while most report decent earnings, some like $ARMADA (5210.MY)$ $VELESTO (5243.MY)$ $WASCO (5142.MY)$ even resume paying dividends after years of hiatus, but seems like market isnt buying it, the outliers seems to be $DELEUM (5132.MY)$ , which is no surprise as they are petronas opex. Along with $HAWK (0320.MY)$ , they tend to be more stable and defensive, wont experience boom during upcycle but wont make losses during downturn
3. Consumers : This was a surprise for me, while the earnings were decent, i personally think this is more of a sentiment thing, a result foreigners selling, this is backed by fundflow data. Consumers tend to be more defensive, you'd expect them to do well even in downturns like now, but as usual, sentiment can affect their valuation, especially for large caps like $MRDIY (5296.MY)$ $99SMART (5326.MY)$, both experience some sort of dump, worst hit was definitely $GENTING (3182.MY)$ $GENM (4715.MY)$, while breweries like $CARLSBG (2836.MY)$ $HEIM (3255.MY)$ did okay, helped by their dividends
Conclusion
Theres a saying that the stock market testing ground both investors and companies, it test companies ability to deliver earnings growth, while it test investors abiity to find and hold good companies. These are trying times, where the men get separated from the boys, wheat gets separated from the chaff so to speak. How and what you do as investor during these times will determine your success or failure.
Overall, out of my 7 holdings, 6/7 have reported earnings, only 1/7 was below expectation, and dumped 30% from the peak, but due to my emphasis on margin of safety, yours truly is only down 10% on that stock. 4/7 declared dividends, one resumption after 10 years, two had record earnings and dividend. I'm expecting 1 more QR at end march, which hopefully will be record earnings as well.
My portfolio is down from the peak in Dec 2024, i expect most people to be no different, in fact its down 9%+ YTD, but still overall in the green when accounted for past capital gains and dividends. As mentioned in previous post, strategy for 2025 is to hold more cash and average in as i see fit. So far, i would like to see more weakenss before i deploy capital, but i also know you cant time the bottom
As usual, none of what i said should be considered as financial advice, always do your own research, any question, feel free to comment below, these are hard times, we need all the support we can get.

title: Genting’s Controlling Shareholders Increase Stakes Amid Share Price Decline
author: Zaclim
body:
’s stock has taken a major hit, dropping 18% to a near 10-year low since its financial results were released in late February. This decline has prompted its controlling shareholders—the Lim family, through Kien Huat Realty and Lim Keong Hui—to increase their holdings.
1. Lim Family Steps In
For the first time in nearly four years, Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay and his family have been actively buying Genting shares:
✅ 7.26 million shares purchased, valued at RM22.86 million
✅ Kien Huat Realty acquired 6 million shares
✅ Lim Keong Hui purchased 1.26 million shares
This move is seen as a vote of confidence in the company’s long-term prospects.
2. Market Reaction & Analyst Views
📉 Despite the recent selloff, Maybank IB Research sees 23% upside for Genting’s stock, alongside a 3% dividend yield.
📈 With valuations at historic lows, the firm has upgraded its rating to “Buy” following the insider acquisitions.
3. What Led to the Decline?
1️⃣ Surprise Q4 Loss – Genting reported a RM169.4 million net loss, its first quarterly loss in two years.
2️⃣ Dividend Cut – The reduction in FY2024 dividend payout led to further selling pressure.
3️⃣ Challenges in Las Vegas – Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV) underperformed due to warm weather and an investigation by the Nevada Gaming Control Board over illegal bookmaking.
4. Leadership Transition: A Turning Point?
Genting has appointed Datuk Seri Tan Kong Han as CEO (effective March 1), taking over from Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay, who remains Executive Chairman. Analysts see this non-family leadership shift as a positive step for corporate governance.
Tan himself recently purchased 100,000 Genting shares worth RM300,000, signaling confidence in the company’s future.
5. Upcoming Catalysts
A key near-term trigger for Genting’s valuation is its 20%-owned TauRx Pharmaceuticals Ltd. By April–June, the company expects a decision from the UK’s Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency on its Alzheimer’s drug.
💰 If approved, TauRx could be valued at US$15 billion, translating to RM5.09 per Genting share, according to Maybank IB Research.
6. Final Thoughts
Despite current challenges, Genting still holds upside potential. With insider buying, leadership changes, and potential breakthroughs in TauRx, investors may find value in the stock’s recovery prospects.

title: CreditSights: The credit outlook for Genting's dual giants is good this year, but bad next year.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 20th) Fitch's CreditSights, a credit market research institution, believes that the demand in the Gambling, Leisure, and Hotel Industry remains robust, thus, Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ and Resorts World Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ The crediting outlook is expected to gradually improve this year.
However, the Institutions also stated that the crediting outlook for Genting Group will worsen next year, mainly due to accelerated investments.
CreditSights analysts noted in a report that supported by strong demand in the gambling, leisure, and hospitality industry, the crediting outlook for Genting and Genting Malaysia is expected to gradually improve by fiscal year 2025 (ending December).
The analysts also predict that the revenue and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) for Genting and Genting Malaysia will increase by 3% to 7% this year.
In terms of capital expenditure, analysts estimate that Genting will only slightly increase investment this year, but next year, influenced by the expansion plans of Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) and Resorts World New York, investments will accelerate.
We expect Genting's free cash flow to come under pressure and turn negative in fiscal year 2026.
Therefore, while the outlook is optimistic this year, the analysts believe that the crediting outlook for Genting and Genting Malaysia may deteriorate next year.
The capital expenditure for Resorts World New York is expected to be substantial, Genting may primarily finance through debt, and the negative impacts brought by this may overshadow the bullish EBITDA profit growth.
Overall, CreditSights has started to track Genting and Genting Malaysia, giving ratings of "Market Perform" and "Outperform" respectively.
Source: Nanyang Siang Pau.

author: Zamm
body:
Comparing Malaysia's tourism industry to that of Macau reveals some differences. Macau's tourism sector has been heavily reliant on gambling, which has faced challenges in recent years. The Macau government has recognized the need for economic diversification and has introduced the "1+4" development strategy to reduce reliance on gambling by promoting industries such as life sciences, financial technology, advanced technology, and large-scale event production. Despite these efforts, Macau continues to face challenges in achieving sustainable growth, partly due to its limited land and human resources.

In contrast, Malaysia's tourism industry is more diversified, encompassing eco-tourism, cultural tourism, medical tourism, and more. This diversification, coupled with ongoing efforts to enhance sustainability and align with ESG principles, positions Malaysia's tourism sector for continued growth leading up to and beyond Visit Malaysia Year 2026.

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | Nestlé Malaysia Invests RM250 Million in New Port Klang Logistics Hub
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Good morning mooers! Here are things you need to know about today's market:
U.S. stocks rose slightly on Friday, despite the first triple-witching day of 2025.
Malaysian stocks ended slightly higher on Friday bucking the regional downtrend.
Stocks to watch: ABMB, CAPITALA, etc.
- Moomoo News MY
Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 5,667.56 (+0.08%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 4,1985.35 (+0.08%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 17,784.05 (+0.52%)
On Friday, despite it being 2025’s first "triple-witching day"—when $4.5 trillion in contracts expire, often sparking volatility as investors rejig portfolios—the Nasdaq Composite Index rallied 0.52% to 17,784.05, bouncing back from earlier dips. The S&P 500 inched up 0.08% to 5,667.56, halting a four-week slide.
Surprisingly, markets remained steady, shrugging off President Trump’s ongoing trade spats with Mexico, Canada, China, and others.
$Boeing (BA.US)$ shares rose 3.1% following news of a major $20 billion contract win to develop the new F-47 fighter jet for the U.S.
$Micron Technology (MU.US)$ dropped 8% after its Q2 results, even though it beat analyst expectations.
$FedEx (FDX.US)$ fell 6.4% following a reduced earnings forecast and lower-than-expected Q3 profit, marking its third consecutive quarterly outlook cut.
Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1505.45 (+0.09%)
Top Gainer: $PETDAG (5681.MY)$ RM19.2 (+9.97%)
Top Loser: $AXIATA (6888.MY)$ RM1.71 (-4.47%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.4210 (-0.04%)
The $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ edged up 0.09% on Friday, closing at 1,505.45, despite regional market weakness. Trading was mixed, with more stocks falling than rising, as investors remained cautious. The index saw a weekly decline of 0.44%, reflecting ongoing market uncertainties and global volatility.
Bursa Malaysia Derivatives is set to relaunch its Single Stock Futures (SSF) contract on March 24, with significant improvements. The revamped SSF will track the 30 largest companies in the FBM KLCI, featuring a reduced contract size of 100 shares and lower initial margins.
Malaysian economists project stable inflation for 2025, with forecasts ranging from 2.3% to 2.6%. The outlook is influenced by global commodity prices, domestic policies, and potential subsidy reforms. February's inflation rate of 1.5% aligns with expectations, though a slight uptick is anticipated later in the year.
Major banks, including RHB, UOB, and CIMB, expect the central bank to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate at 3% throughout 2025.
IPO Scanner
Stocks to Watch
$ABMB (2488.MY)$ is set to bolster its capital with a planned rights issue of up to RM600 million. The funds will support the bank's core operations, including lending and investment activities. While details on share pricing are pending, major shareholder Vertical Theme Sdn Bhd has committed to fully subscribe to its 29.06% entitlement, signaling strong support for the initiative.
$CAPITALA (5099.MY)$ has received High Court approval for its share capital reduction, clearing the path for a proposed distribution to shareholders. CEO Tony Fernandes emphasized the importance of this step in streamlining the company's structure. The exact reduction amount will be determined based on $AAX (5238.MY)$'s share price, as Capital A aims to refocus on its travel and digital business segments.
$NESTLE (4707.MY)$ has initiated construction on a RM250 million logistics hub in Port Klang. Set to open in early 2026, the facility will serve as a regional center for exports to over 60 countries and handle raw material imports. The project is expected to create more than 200 jobs and forms part of Nestlé's strategy to enhance supply chain efficiency and sustainability.
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ has agreed to a US$10.5 million settlement with Nevada gaming regulators over a complaint against its Las Vegas resort. If approved by the Nevada Gaming Commission on March 27, 2025, this would represent one of the largest fines in the state's gaming history. The agreement involves Resorts World Las Vegas LLC and aims to resolve regulatory issues at the property.
$VS (6963.MY)$'s Q2 FY2025 net profit fell 4% to RM15.38 million, mainly due to lower forex gains. Revenue rose slightly by 2.8% to RM908.79 million. The Malaysian segment showed strong growth, while Singapore and Indonesian operations declined. Despite mixed results, the company declared a 0.4 sen dividend per share.

title: Foreigners Flee Malaysian Banks, but Locals Dive In: What's the Deal?
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Hey everyone!
The markets have been on a rollercoaster ride again this week. Foreigners are still pulling out of Malaysian banks, but locals are stepping in. Let's take a closer look at what's going on.
Market Pulse: Global Economy in Turbulence
Interest Rates and Economic Data
The US Fed kept rates steady at 4.25–4.50%, but hinted at cuts later. Core PCE inflation eased to 2.6% YoY in Jan-25. The US budget deficit hit a record $1.15t in the first five months of FY25.
Market Reactions
Most global indices were up. India's Sensex soared 4.17%, while Indonesia's JCI tanked 3.95%. The US dollar depreciated against the Ringgit by 0.58%, and Brent crude rose 2.24% to $72.16/barrel.
Market Sentiment
Uncertainty is high. Investors are cautious due to inflation, trade tensions, and geopolitical issues.
Asia’s Money Moves: Inflows and Outflows Galore
Overall Fund Flows
Foreign investors sold a total of -$564.9m in 8 Asian markets for the 4th week straight. Only South Korea ($1.68b) and the Philippines ($40.1m) saw inflows.
Standout Markets
South Korea reversed nine weeks of outflows. Its chemical firms are shifting focus due to China's competition.
Taiwan had a net outflow of -$1.12b for four weeks, with its central bank keeping rates high.
Driving Forces
Geopolitical tensions, trade policies, and economic fundamentals are influencing money flows.
Malaysia Breakdown
Foreigners Keep Selling
Foreigners sold RM1.25b for the 22nd week in a row, mainly offloading Financial Services (-RM609.7m). Wednesday was the worst day, with an outflow of RM484.23m. Thankfully, compared with last week, foreign investors are no longer selling a large number of shares of $GENTING (3182.MY)$.
Local Show Support
Local institutions bought RM1.23b, while local retail investors added RM25.5m. This shows locals are more confident in the domestic market.
Sectoral Trends
The Plantation sector saw a tiny inflow of RM2.4m. Financial, Industrial, and Consumer sectors faced selling pressure.
Stock Spotlight: Who’s Buying What?
Big Trades: $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$, $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$, and $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ had significant direct business transactions.
Strategy Breakdown: Why the Different Moves?
Foreign Investors
Foreigners have a global view and more sensitivity to international risks. They're dumping Malaysian banks due to global risks and looking for safer havens. Concerns about trade and inflation are driving their decisions.
Local Institutions
Locals may have better knowledge of domestic conditions, and their funds are often for the long term. They favor banks like $CIMB (1023.MY)$ and $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ for long term value and stable dividends. It's a bet on Malaysia's domestic economic strength.
Local Retail Investors
They chase hot stocks like $CIMB (1023.MY)$, but their trading volume is small and more speculative. They might be influenced by short term market news.
We all know that 2024 was a highlight year for the Malaysian stock market. Which companies were the most favored by foreign investors in that year? How are their stock prices performing now?
In 2024, foreign investors made substantial purchases of $TENAGA (5347.MY)$. As of February 25 this year, foreign ownership in $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ accounted for 17.6%. $MAHSING (8583.MY)$ rose 124% in 2024 and became the best performing company among the targets with net foreign capital inflows. The average return of the top 5 targets with net inflows is 61.23%.
Risks to Watch
1）Tariff disputes could escalate, disrupting global trade.
2）Central bank policies might change unexpectedly, affecting markets.

title: Genting approved by NGC hearing and reached a settlement with the Nevada Gaming Commission.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, Oct 28) Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ announced that the Nevada Gaming Commission (NGC) approved the company's settlement agreement with the Nevada Gaming Control Board (NGCB) at a hearing.
On Friday, Genting reported to the Malaysian Stock Exchange that the settlement and order were approved at a hearing by the Nevada Gaming Commission on March 27 (Las Vegas time).
Looking back at the earlier report on March 21, Genting disclosed that it reached a settlement with the Nevada Gaming Control Board (NGCB) and paid a fine of 10.5 million USD (approximately 46.41 million Ringgit) to conclude the regulatory turmoil.
Genting's wholly-owned Las Vegas Genting World (RWLV) signed the settlement agreement and related order with NGCB on March 20.
The settlement agreement was jointly signed by RWLV Holdings, Genting Assets, Suasana Duta, and Peak Avenue, among other entities, which were previously complained about by NGCB on August 15, 2024.
At that time, Genting also emphasized that RWLV had actively communicated with NGCB to resolve the related complaints and had implemented remedial measures, including enhancing the anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program and making major management adjustments.
RWLV emphasizes that the company is committed to complying with all Gambling regulations and has optimized its internal compliance system to ensure future adherence to regulatory requirements.

body:
Good morning mooers! Here are things you need to know about today's market:
U.S. stocks had a mixed performance on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 rising, while the Dow edged lower.
Malaysian stocks fell on Friday due to global trade concerns, following market closures on Monday and Tuesday for Hari Raya Aidilfitri.
Stocks to watch: YINSON, MNHLDG, etc.
- Moomoo News MY
Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 5,633.07 (+0.38%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 4,1989.96 (-0.03%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 17,449.89 (+0.87%)
US markets showed mixed results Tuesday, with tech-heavy Nasdaq and broad-based S&P 500 gaining ground, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slightly retreated.
Investors are cautious as President Trump prepares to unveil major import tariffs on Wednesday, which he calls "Liberation Day", at 4 p.m. ET, coinciding with the NYSE and Nasdaq closing.
Investors are concerned about potential trade wars and their impact on US stocks, inflation, and economic growth. While details remain unclear, sources suggest a possible 20% tariff on most imports.
Adding to market uncertainty, recent economic data disappointed. The March ISM Manufacturing Index came in at 49.0, below expectations, and February's job openings fell to 7.57 million, lower than anticipated.
Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1513.65 (-1.44%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.4375 (+0.01%)
Malaysian markets were closed on Monday, March 31, and Tuesday, April 1, for Hari Raya Aidilfitri celebrations.
Malaysian stocks fell Friday, mirroring losses in Asian markets. The $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ dropped 22.08 points to 1,513.65. The broader market faced downward pressure amid global trade concerns.
A Petronas gas pipeline explosion in Putra Heights, Subang Jaya disrupted Aidilfitri celebrations on Tuesday, damaging 190 homes. The national oil company confirmed the incident, stating they've isolated the affected pipeline and alerted authorities.
In March 2025, the Malaysian Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.8 from 49.7, marking the tenth consecutive month of sector contraction. New orders declined modestly, reversing previous growth.
Global trade uncertainty led to weaker international demand. Production and employment decreased, while backlogs of work reduced.
From April 1, Mida is launching a new Investor Pass for foreign investors in Malaysia. This pass allows a six-month stay, extendable for another six months.
Malaysia's Department of Statistics reported a slight increase in trade prices for February. Export prices edged up 0.1% to 151.2 points, while import prices saw a 0.3% rise to 128.1 points. The import price increase was primarily driven by mineral fuels.
IPO Scanner
Stocks to Watch
$MNHLDG (0245.MY)$ secured a RM137.8 million contract from $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ for a 275kV switching station in Terengganu. This is their largest direct contract from TNB, increasing their order book to RM977.8 million.
Nevada Gaming Commission approved $GENTING (3182.MY)$'s US$10.5 million settlement for a complaint against its Las Vegas resort.
$LSH (0351.MY)$ denies claims in a lawsuit by the former KL Tower operator. The company states its subsidiary won the contract through a legitimate government procurement process.
$YINSON (7293.MY)$' Q4 net profit fell to RM146 million from RM278 million year-on-year. Revenue decreased to RM1.4 billion. The company cites lower EPCIC contribution and higher costs. A final dividend of one sen per share was declared.
Auditors have raised red flags about $SCABLE (5170.MY)$'s financial health for the third year running. The PN17 company's ability to continue operating is in doubt, according to its external auditors.

title: taurx 9/4/2025
author: KENGRACING
body: Researchers reported a potential oral treatment for Alzheimer's disease that slows its progression for at least 18 months. Developed by the Singapore company TauRx Pharmaceutics Ltd, scientists based in Aberdeen report that if approved by regulatory Institutions, Methylthiohydroxy (HMTM) could be the first oral treatment for Alzheimer's disease (AD) targeting tau protein pathology. These findings were announced on Saturday at the major international conference AD/PD 2025 held in Vienna. During the event, TauRx Pharmaceuticals' CEO and co-founder Professor Claude Wischik outlined work comparing the results of the recent Phase 3 trials of HMTM with placebo data from closely matched subjects available in the Alzheimer's Disease Critical Path (CPAD) database, which contains information from nearly 10,000 patients participating in 36 Global trials. Professor Wischik, who leads this research, said: "In three different analyses comparing HMTM with external data, the results were consistent, indicating that HMTM effectively reduces clinical decline and brain atrophy progression for at least 18 months, with the potential clinical significance of treatment effects lasting up to two years." "We believe HMTM has the potential to become a safe and accessible oral treatment option for early to mild/moderate AD, which can be provided with minimal burden on patients and doctors." "Although this is not a cure, research indicates that starting HMTM treatment early in the disease can significantly delay progression. As demonstrated in trials involving over 3,000 patients, the strong safety profile combined with oral administration leads us to believe that we have a medication that people can take just like other prescription drugs." TauRx has submitted a marketing authorization application for HMTM to the United Kingdom's Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), and the company is also collaborating with the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) to assess whether the drug is suitable for use in the NHS. Using the ADAS-cog13 scoring system, which measures the ability to recall words and perform tasks such as memory tests, it indicates that patients with early disease taking HMTM did not experience a significant decline from baseline scores over 18 months, in contrast to a substantial drop in the CPAD placebo data. In addition, an examination of the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) scale used for global assessment of dementia severity showed similar results, with the progression of brain atrophy being an objective indicator of neurodegeneration, significantly reduced in the HMTM data. Since the discovery of Alzheimer's disease in 1988, which is composed of abnormally assembled tau proteins that form destructive filaments within brain nerve cells, tau proteins have been at the forefront of research. While several other drugs focus on amyloid proteins, HMTM works differently as it targets the abnormal assembly of tau proteins. It is also the only oral tau therapy to complete Phase 3 trials.

title: On the 26th of next month, the semi-annual review will take place, and the constituent stocks are expected to remain unchanged. Mr. DIY has some concerns.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
On the 26th of next month, a semi-annual review is expected, and the constituent stocks are likely to remain unchanged. Mr. DIY has some concerns.
In the upcoming semi-annual review of the constituent stocks, analysts predict that for the first time in three years, 30 index constituent stocks will remain unchanged.
According to the research report from MIDF Investment Bank, the newly included GEM will be evaluated in the December 2024 constituent stock review.$GAMUDA(5398.MY)$ And 99 Speed Mart.$99SMART(5326.MY)$ Currently, the position in the Index is stable, and there is no risk of being replaced.
The deadline for the next round of component stock reviews is May 26, 2025.
MIDF stated: "Currently, no Stocks have a Market Cap that meets or falls below the criteria for inclusion or exclusion."
According to FTSE Index rules, Stocks that want to be included in the Index must rank in the top 25 by Market Cap, and if the Market Cap falls to 36th place or lower, they may be excluded.
Meanwhile, Stocks must also have at least a 15% public shareholding ratio to qualify for evaluation.
MIDF pointed out that despite recent market fluctuations due to the new round of tariffs by Trump and subsequent policy pauses, the overall impact is broad, without causing significant changes in the Market Cap rankings of individual companies.
Currently, the company closest to the inclusion threshold is Maybank.$AMBANK(1015.MY)$ It ranks 28th in Market Cap.
KPJ is expected to enter the reserve list.
Despite being 3.2% lower in Market Cap compared to the 25th place, Quanli Resources,$QL(7084.MY)$ MIDF believes that this gap is "difficult to close" in the short term.
If this gap is unexpectedly broken, Mr. DIY, currently ranked 33rd,$MRDIY(5296.MY)$ may face the risk of being removed.
In the short term, the most likely change is that Johor Medical Healthcare$KPJ(5878.MY)$ will be included in the candidate list, replacing the delisted Malaysia Airports.
The remaining candidates include Genting.$GENTING(3182.MY)$ Joint planting.$UTDPLT(2089.MY)$ And Westport Holdings.$WPRTS(5246.MY)$ 。
According to estimates of the top 40 stocks as of last Friday, all stocks meet the requirement of more than 15% free float, with the only exception being the City Center Industry.$KLCC(5235SS.MY)$ 。
The Index target has been revised down to 1590 points.
On the other hand, given the current rise in macro risks, especially the uncertainty brought by the USA tariff plans, MIDF Investment Bank has recently lowered its target for the FTSE Long Index in 2025 from the original 1670 points to 1590 points, with the price-earnings ratio also decreasing from 14.8 times to 14.2 times.
Analysts pointed out that under the current environment, market valuations are expected to remain under pressure, making significant recovery difficult.
However, despite lowering the GDP growth forecast for 2025 to 4.0%, Malaysia's economic fundamentals remain robust.
Under the adjusted GDP benchmark forecast, MIDF Investment Bank still expects the Index constituent companies to achieve a 5.6% annual earnings growth rate in 2025, demonstrating relatively healthy growth momentum.

title: After foreign capital net sold Malaysian stocks 0.33 billion, signs of stabilization are emerging.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 21) The trend of foreign capital net selling in the Malaysian stock market has continued for the 26th week, but the outflow momentum has somewhat eased, with a net sale of 0.3 billion Ringgit last week.
MIDF research pointed out in its Capital Trend report that foreign investors continued to sell Malaysian stocks during the first four trading days of last week, with the largest sell-off occurring on Wednesday, recording a net sale of 0.1 billion Ringgit.
However, entering Friday, foreign investors finally returned to the Malaysian market, with a net purchase of 39.9 million Ringgit in one day.
The sectors that experienced the highest net foreign selling last week were financial services (-96.6 million Ringgit), Technology (-87 million Ringgit), and construction (-80.8 million Ringgit).
At the same time, the sectors with the highest net inflow from foreign capital last week were telecommunications and media (0.1 billion Ringgit), consumer products and services (34.4 million Ringgit), and industrials (2.45 million Ringgit).
Local Institutions continue to support the Ask from foreign investors, net buying Malaysian stocks for 26 consecutive weeks, with a net purchase amount of 0.3 billion Ringgit.
Local retail investors are beginning to move against local Institutions, with a net Sell of 25.7 million Ringgit in Malaysian stocks last week.
In terms of participation, the average daily trading volume (ADTV) of Malaysian stocks fell last week. The trading volume for foreign investors, local Institutions, and retail investors decreased by 48.7%, 56.7%, and 47.2% respectively.

title: Will there be a stock market crash in the next two years.
author: 旋风小肥侠
body:
The risk of a significant stock market crash occurring in the next two years is notably present, but it is not inevitable. The key factors depend on:
- Whether the valuation of the US stock market can be digested through earnings growth;
- Whether the Federal Reserve's policies can timely respond to the economic slowdown;
- Whether geopolitical conflicts escalate into a systemic crisis.

2. **Investor strategy**
- **Defensive allocation**: Focus on companies with low debt and stable cash flow, or long-term growth areas such as the GREEN ECONOMY.
- **Diversify risk**: Increase non-US Assets (such as Emerging Markets, CSI Commodity Equity Index) to hedge against US stock volatility.
- **Avoid excessive leverage**: History shows that high leverage is a major cause of amplified losses during crashes.

In summary, the market may experience severe fluctuations or even phased crashes in the next two years, but whether a comprehensive major stock market crash occurs will depend on policy responses and Global economic resilience. Investors need to remain cautious of risks while avoiding overreactions and maintaining a long-term perspective.

title: Genting's first quarter profit plummeted from last year's 0.5887 billion Ringgit to 4.5 million Ringgit.
author: 旋风小肥侠
body: Kuala Lumpur: Genting Berhad's net income for the first quarter ending March 31, 2025, plummeted to 4.57 million Ringgit from 0.58887 billion Ringgit a year ago. The group's revenue was 6.51 billion Ringgit, a 12% decrease compared to 7.43 billion Ringgit in the same period last year. Genting attributed the decline in revenue primarily to the leisure and hotel sectors. The group's adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (Ebitda) for the first quarter of 2025 was 1.99 billion Ringgit, down from 2.57 billion Ringgit in the first quarter of 2024. The strengthening of the Ringgit against the Singapore Dollar, British Pound, and US Dollar contributed to the decline in the group's revenue and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. Genting stated that the revenue and profits of Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) have both decreased. The performance for the first quarter of 2025 was affected by a lower VIP rolling win rate and the temporary closure of the Hard Rock Hotel for renovations and rebranding, which resulted in a reduction in available room inventory. Compared to the first quarter of 2024, the performance of Resorts World Sentosa was also weaker due to an increase in the number of tourists and tourism spending in Singapore during the Lunar New Year holiday, and the relaxation of visa regulations between China and Singapore in February 2024. Due to the festive season and a decline in high-end player business volume, the revenue of Genting World (RWG) decreased compared to the first quarter of 2024. Due to the strengthening of the Ringgit against the British Pound, the group's revenues from leisure and hotel businesses in the United Kingdom and Egypt have declined. However, the lower EBITDA was mainly due to increased operational and payroll-related costs in the first quarter of 2025. The financial performance of leisure and hotel businesses in the United States and the Bahamas includes Resorts World New York City (RWNYC), Resorts World Bimini (RW Bimini), and Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV). Due to the strengthening of the Ringgit against the US Dollar, the revenue of RWNYC has declined. Compared to the record traffic brought by the NFL Super Bowl event in the first quarter of 2024, RWLV's revenue and EBITDA were affected by a lower Hold and lower foot traffic. In the first quarter of 2025, the hotel occupancy rate was 82.3%, with an average daily rate of 274 US dollars, while in the first quarter of 2024, it was 89.1% and 298 US dollars respectively. Genting stated that the performance for the remainder of fiscal year 2025 may be affected by global economic conditions and market fluctuations. Due to escalating geopolitical tensions continuing to affect domestic and global sentiment, it is expected that Malaysia's economic growth will slow down. Although global uncertainty persists, it is expected that international tourism demand will remain resilient, although the recovery will be uneven across regions. Therefore, the regional Gambling market may face increasing challenges, the report added. In Malaysia, the group continues to enhance RWG's attractiveness as a regional tourism hub by introducing new facilities and attractions, including offering new eco-tourism experiences at Genting Highlands. The Genting Group added: "The celebrations for the group's 60th anniversary are ongoing, including various special events, promotions, and activities aimed at attracting visitors and enriching their experience at Genting Highlands."

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | KLSE Dips for 4th Day; Bursa Malaysia Signs MOU to Promote Foreign ETFs Listings
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Good morning mooers! Here are things you need to know about today's market:
U.S. Three Major Indexes Inch Higher
Malaysian Stock Market Dips for Fourth Consecutive Day
Bursa Malaysia Partners to Expand Foreign ETF Listings
Stocks to watch: SUNCON, IHH, etc.
- Moomoo News MY
Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 5,912.17 (+0.40%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 42,215.73 (+0.28%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 19,175.87 (+0.39%)
U.S. stock indexes edged up slightly on Thursday, responding to the latest twist in the legal saga surrounding President Trump's "Liberation Day" tariffs.
The court ordered the tariffs to be nullified, potentially upending a cornerstone of Trump's trade policy. However, this decision was quickly countered by the U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, which issued a stay on the lower court's ruling.
This temporary suspension means the tariffs will remain in effect while the appellate court conducts a more thorough review of the case.
Investors have consistently welcomed any news that could delay or reduce Trump's tariffs, as evidenced by sharp rises in major stock index futures following the initial court ruling against the tariffs.
This positive market reaction reflects widespread concern among investors about the potential economic fallout from these trade measures. Many fear that the tariffs, combined with foreign retaliation, could lead to higher inflation and unemployment in the US.
The Bureau of Economic Analysis provided a modestly positive update on the U.S. economy Thursday, revising its first-quarter GDP estimate. The new figures show the economy contracted at a 0.2% annual rate, an improvement from the previously reported 0.3% decline.
This slight upward revision, while still indicating economic contraction, offers a glimmer of hope for Wall Street and investors.The adjusted data suggests that the economic slowdown in the first quarter was not as severe as initially thought, potentially signaling more resilience in the U.S. economy than previously believed.
NVIDIA, as the key member of the "Mag-7" stocks, saw its shares climb 3.25% during Thursday's trading session. This significant rise came after the company reported better-than-expected first-quarter earnings and revenues, surpassing analyst estimates.
Conversely, Alphabet and Apple experienced minor declines on Thursday. Alphabet shares dropped 0.29%, while Apple fell 0.23%.
Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1518.980 (-0.30%)
Top Gainer: $PETDAG (5681.MY)$ RM20.500 (+1.49%)
Top Loser: $TM (4863.MY)$ RM6.590 (-3.80%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.2440 (+0.45%)
The FBM KLCI continued its downward trajectory for the fourth consecutive session, closing 0.3% lower at 1,518.98. This performance stood in contrast to the broader Asian market rally, which was buoyed by a U.S. trade court's decision to block President Trump's tariffs.
Trading was relatively balanced with 466 gainers, 478 losers, and 460 unchanged stocks. The market saw a volume of 3.3 billion shares traded, valued at RM2.22 billion.
Dealers anticipate continued lackluster market conditions in the near term, citing ongoing tariff concerns and a lack of strong domestic catalysts as factors that may keep investors cautious.
Additionally, Bursa Malaysia Bhd, Fullgoal Asset Management (HK) Ltd, and CGS International Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd have signed a memorandum of understanding to facilitate the listing of foreign-underlying exchange-traded funds (ETFs) on Bursa Malaysia.
This collaboration aims to provide Malaysian investors with access to a wider range of investment options and exposure to global markets.
The agreement, signed at the ASEAN Business Forum 2025, reflects a joint commitment to promote capital market connectivity between China and Malaysia, enrich cross-border product offerings, and enhance the asset management industry's development capabilities.
IPO Scanner
ASM Automation Group Bhd plans to raise RM21.82 million through an IPO on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market. The company will issue 128.34 million new shares at 17 sen each, representing 24% of its enlarged share capital. Proceeds from the IPO will be used for business expansion in the automation machinery sector.
Stocks to Watch
$SUNCON (5263.MY)$ has secured two significant contracts totaling RM1.16 billion from a leading US technology company. The projects, set to commence immediately and conclude by February 2027, involve general contractor services for data center construction.
$IHH (5225.MY)$ experienced a 33% decrease in net profit for Q1 2025, dropping to RM514 million. This decline was primarily due to accounting adjustments and the absence of a one-time tax credit from the previous year.
$KPJ (5878.MY)$ reported a 20% year-on-year decrease in net profit for Q1 2025, earning RM57.06 million. The decline was attributed to losses in overseas operations and the absence of contributions from discontinued Australian operations.
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ saw a significant drop in net profit for Q1 2025, falling to just RM4.57 million from RM588.87 million a year earlier. This sharp decline was accompanied by a 12.4% decrease in revenue, which totaled RM6.51 billion.
$GENM (4715.MY)$ reported a 25.69% year-on-year increase in net profit for Q1 2025, reaching RM72.58 million. This improvement was primarily due to foreign exchange gains and better cost management.
$CHINHIN (5273.MY)$'s Q1 net profit doubled to RM18.39 million, driven by contributions from Signature International Bhd and a turnaround in its property development segment. Revenue surged 66.9% to RM951.95 million.
$TROP (5401.MY)$ reported a net profit of RM1.32 million in Q1 2025, marking its second consecutive profitable quarter. This result was supported by a tax credit of RM6.63 million. However, quarterly revenue decreased by 10.61% to RM260.36 million due to lower recurring income following property disposals.
