title: Heavy selling pressure · a continuous decline. Profit storm stocks face harsh conditions.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 30th) Several listed companies saw their stock prices plummet sharply during the morning trading session due to earnings performance falling short of market expectations, among which, Genting's twin companies became the market focus.
Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ On Thursday, it announced a 99% year-on-year decline in net profit for the first quarter of the 2025 fiscal year, significantly below market expectations, causing the stock price to open lower on Friday.
As of noon trading, the stock price plummeted by 3.8% or 12 cents, reaching a low of 3.01 Ringgit for the day, marking a new low since early April.
At the same time, it also dragged down Genting Malaysia. $GENM (4715.MY)$ This morning, it briefly dropped by 1.1% to 1.80 Ringgit, despite recording a 25.6% year-on-year growth in net profit for the first quarter.
This is not the first time Genting has faced a significant drop in stock price due to poor performance. In February this year, Genting announced a loss for the end of the fiscal year 2024, which triggered panic in the market, causing the stock price to plunge nearly 12% the following day.
At that time, Genting Malaysia, which also reported a loss, saw an even greater drop, plummeting 19.5% in a single day, directly falling below the 2 Ringgit level.
Genting is undervalued.
Today, in light of the performance being below expectations, Galaxy International Securities has lowered its earnings forecast and Target Price for Genting to 3.57 Ringgit, but still maintains a 'Shareholding' rating, believing the valuation is undervalued.
Analysts state that the investment logic for Genting remains unchanged and still considers it an effective Indicator for the number of visitors from Malaysia and Singapore.
On the other hand, analysts expect Genting Malaysia to invest higher operating and capital expenditures in the fiscal years 2025 and 2026 for New York's Resorts World (RWNYC) in preparation for the bid for the downstate casino license in New York City, which may lead to a contraction in profit margins and could even reduce dividend payouts.
Therefore, analysts have downgraded the rating for Genting Malaysia from 'Shareholding' to 'Hold' and have cut the Target Price to 1.88 Ringgit.
Ajinomoto Rarely Incurs Losses.
In addition, Ajinomoto $AJI (2658.MY)$ has rarely reported a loss, causing its stock price to drop significantly on Friday, falling as much as 11% or 1.56 Ringgit during the session, reaching 12.68 Ringgit, marking a new low since June 2023.
Ajinomoto reported a loss of 6.9 million Ringgit at the end of the fiscal year 2025 (ending March) mainly due to increased selling and administrative expenses.
Following closely is the Johor Medical Health, which also reported disappointing performance. $KPJ (5878.MY)$ This morning, it once dropped to 2.67 Ringgit, with a decline of 9.8%.
In the first quarter of the 2025 fiscal year (ending March), Johor Medical Health's net profit fell by 20% year-on-year to 57.06 million Ringgit, mainly due to losses in overseas business and the gap left by the cessation of operations in Australia.
Given that the performance in the first quarter only accounted for 16% of the full-year forecast, Hong Leong Investment Bank has revised down the earnings forecasts for the fiscal years 2025 and 2026 by 8.6% and 7.8%, respectively.
Qianli Resources' net profit slows down.
In contrast, Qianli Resources, which has always performed brilliantly, $QL (7084.MY)$ after 11 consecutive quarters of net profit growth, recorded a slowdown in growth for the first time, leading to selling pressure on its stock price, which fell by 2% or 9 cents to 4.45 Ringgit, a relatively light decline.
For the end of the 2025 fiscal year, Qianli Resources earned a net profit of 93.92 million Ringgit, a year-on-year decrease of 4.92%; revenues recorded 1.7 billion 61.4 million Ringgit, with a year-on-year growth of 6.74%.
Analysts from the bank's investment research believe that fishery product manufacturing (MPM) remains a key source of profit in the coming period, but as the egg subsidy will be fully removed on August 1, the profitability of integrated livestock farming (ILF) may weaken due to sluggish prices and increased supply.
Analysts indicated that the net profit for the year only reached 93% of expectations, thus lowering the forecasts for the fiscal years 2026 and 2027 by 11% to 15%.
The net profit of Zhenke plummeted by 96%.
Zhenke, which also fell due to a poor performance report. $GENETEC (0104.MY)$ This morning, it dropped below the Ringgit 1 level, at one point falling 7% to 98.5 cents, hitting a new low in three weeks.
This contract manufacturer of automation industrial equipment saw its net profit in the third quarter of fiscal year 2025 plummet by 96% year-on-year, earning only 0.759 million Ringgit.
Analysts at Galaxy International Securities maintained their 'Shareholding' rating, keeping the Target Price at 81 cents unchanged, considering factors such as the rising client concentration risk, weak global demand for electric vehicles, and the poor demand outlook caused by uncertainties surrounding US tariffs.
Kucingko once plummeted by 18%.
As for the "cat stock" Kucingko company that has been listed for less than a year, $KUCINGKO (0315.MY)$ the financial performance for the first quarter of the 2025 fiscal year was disappointing, and the stock price immediately fell by 18% or 2.5 sen to 11.5 sen on Friday.
This animation company announced its performance on Thursday, with first-quarter revenue plummeting by 97% to 0.21 million Ringgit, and turning from profit to a loss of 3.68 million Ringgit.
Source: Nanyang Siang Pau.

title: The performance in the first quarter is frequently alarming, and the 1500 support is in jeopardy.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
The performance of enterprises in the first quarter has dimmed, market sentiment remains weak, and the Malaysian stock market has seen a continuous decline for half a month since May 15, putting the 1500 support point at risk. On the first trading day of June, the pessimistic sentiment in the Malaysian stock market persists,$FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ The FTSE Bursa Malaysia Composite Index briefly fell below 1500 points during the morning session today, reaching a low of 1497.42 points; however, due to investors taking advantage of the lower prices to buy in, the index was pushed back above the key support level.
Today the morning trading session was closed, the FTSE RINGS index reported at 1503.46 points, down 4.89 points or 0.32%; meanwhile, most Asian stock markets showed an upward trend in the morning. Since the peak of 1586.85 points on May 15, the Malaysian stock market has fallen by 5.26% in half a month. There has only been one day of increase in 13 trading days, and it has now experienced six consecutive declines.
Performance disasters in certain industries. The research analyst at CIMB Investment Bank pointed out that the performance was worse than expected, affecting various Industries, especially in the Oil and Gas, Consumer Goods, Technology, and Bank sectors. As a result, the analyst has revised the core net profit growth forecast for the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI for this year and next year from the original 9.3% and 6.6% down to 3.4% and 6.5%. The index target is 1560. Not only that, analysts have also downgraded the SSE Conglomerates Index target from the original 1657 points to 1560 points. Analysts indicated that there are still multiple downward risks affecting market trends, including uncertainties regarding tariffs, which are expected to continue disrupting the market in the third quarter of this year. Furthermore, the Malaysian government may promote targeted RON95 RBOB Gasoline subsidies within this year and higher electricity charges, therefore, analysts continue to view recent trends with caution. Analysts also pointed out that despite multiple downward risks, there are still Bullish trends worth noting, which may offset the downward factors. These include strong domestic liquidity.$USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ The strengthening of the Ringgit, the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), the Johor-Singapore XINJINGJI Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), and the New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP 2030) are policies expected to partially mitigate adverse factors.

title: When the stock price of a well-known company drops significantly, it is an opportunity to Buy at a low price * The Concept of promoting good products.
author: 风起云涌LBF
body:
1~ When you think it is good~ even if the price is a bit high now, you will still feel it is worth Buy... This thinking is not wrong.

2~ When you think it is good~ and you hope it will be lower than the current price before you buy... This logical thinking is also correct.

When it comes to investing and trading stocks, it is essential to recognize that there are no stocks in the world that only increase in price and never decrease. Even the best and most outstanding companies will experience stock price fluctuations like a roller coaster due to economic cycles and market supply and demand (this is a fact. Even the supposedly unbreakable Malaysian Bank MAYBANK saw its price drop to 2.5 during the 2008 U.S. subprime mortgage crisis and the global financial tsunami).

Next, you need to think about what buying stocks can bring you (what we want is returns). #Stable high dividends (at least higher than fixed-term deposits) #Buy low and sell high (earning returns from price differences)... However, so-called good companies do not necessarily meet these two conditions (after years of ups and downs in the stock market, you will definitely discover that many companies with good performance and sound operations may not provide favorable trading opportunities for buy low sell high or high dividends, such as Guo Lingcan's Guocoland properties GUOCO, 1503).

Therefore, data, literature, and what is reflected on the balance sheet *high-quality stocks and good companies do not necessarily suit *small shareholders' entries into the market. This investment and financial management blind spot requires constant reflection (similar to GUOCO types...)

body:
It has everything.. just look at your stock classification.
Assuming a principal of 10K.
I usually invest 5K in blue-chip stocks that have a stable dividend record, such as GENM~SPTOTO~MAGNUM (these will be held for a long time~ the purpose is to receive regular dividends).

I allocate 3K to buy some stocks that I believe have potential, like PANTECH (..2020.. during 2022)~ recently I bought PTRB (East Coast Refrigeration), planning to hold it for at least three years, and when I have money and the stock price adjusts, I'll add more.

As for the 2K, it depends on what opportunities the market presents; occasionally I enter for short-term trading~ for example, recently waiting for KLCI because of the Israel-Iran war, it might drop below 1500~ so I'm eyeing the conversion price of 1450 for the FBMKLCI's CR (CALL WARRANT)~ if I earn enough to meet my Target Price, I'll take profits.

#Big V Strategy 5-3-2 Rule* fundamentally Jun Long.

title: Genting’s High-Roller Ambition: What’s at Stake in New York’s Casino Race
author: Zaclim
body:
is making a bold bet to secure one of three full-scale casino licenses in New York City, aiming to upgrade its existing Resorts World NYC. This high-stakes race could be a transformative catalyst for the gaming giant.
The Potential Payoff: The Bull Case 1. The Goal: Upgrade its current slot machine facility to a full-fledged integrated resort with table games. 2. Massive Revenue Potential: Projects US$2.2B in annual revenue from the NY property by 2027 if successful, rivaling top global casinos. 3. Key Advantage: "Speed to market." As an existing operator, it has a head start over competitors proposing brand-new sites.
The Hurdles & Global Picture: The Bear Case 1. Fierce Competition: It's up against 7 other groups, including gaming giants like MGM and Caesars. 2. Cautious Market: Despite a healthy recovery at its other global properties (Malaysia, Singapore, Las Vegas), Genting's share price is down ~17% YTD, reflecting investor caution. 3. Significant Risks: The upgrade requires huge capex, and uncertainties remain around final tax rates and regulatory approvals.
Investor Outlook: This is a high-risk, high-reward play. Winning the license would be a game-changer, likely triggering a major re-rating of the stock. The decision, expected by December 2025, is the single most significant catalyst on the horizon.
Until then, the stock remains a speculative but compelling wager on one of the biggest prizes in the global gaming industry.

title: a series of setbacks
author: 风起云涌LBF
body:
(Geneva, 9th) The latest release of theMSCI Malaysia Indexhas resulted in the removal of three Malaysian constituents!

According to the announcement by MSCI, the stocks that have been removed from the Malaysia index areGenting(GENTING, 3182, Main Market Consumer Goods)PPB Group(PPB, 4065, Main Market Consumer Goods), andSime Darby(SIME, 4197, Main Market Consumer Goods).

The latest adjustments will take effect after the market closes on August 26.

According to the MSCI's Asia-Pacific adjustment data, Malaysia will have no new additions in this round of adjustments, but three stocks will be removed.

This implies that the affected stocks may face pressure from outflows of funds from passive funds (such as ETFs tracking the MSCI index), potentially leading to short-term downward pressure on their share prices.

Analysts note that MSCI index adjustments typically influence the direction of international capital allocation. Stocks removed from the index may experience passive selling before the effective date.

Additionally, a reduction in the overall market weight could also diminish Malaysia's visibility in international investment portfolios.

title: Foreign Investors Dump Malaysian Stocks as Locals Gobble Up – Weekly Fund Flow Showdown
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Last week was a wild ride with factory strength boosting global markets, but policy gaps and fragile growth kept tensions high. While Asia bled $5.08b in foreign outflows, Malaysia's FBM KLCI defied the trend with a 1.34% weekly gain. But can local investors outmuscle the global sell-off?
Market Pulse: Factory Boom Meets Trade Turmoil
U.S. manufacturing PMI surged to 53.3 in August—its highest since May 2022—defying contraction fears! But new U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminum products (like wind turbines and bulldozers) sparked trade jitters. The Eurozone PMI reached a 15-month high of 51.1, while UK inflation surged to 3.80%, fueling concerns about a rate hike. Markets reacted: Shenzhen CSI 300 jumped 4.18%, but tariffs weighed on Japan's Nikkei (-1.72%). Overall, sentiment is cautious—growth optimism clashes with trade risks, keeping volatility alive.
Asia's Money Moves: Outflows Dominate
Foreign investors bailed out of Asia, with a net outflow of -USD5.08b ending two weeks of inflows! Indonesia was the lone bright spot, pulling in USD167.9m as its central bank cut rates to 5.0%. Elsewhere, South Korea saw USD745.9m outflows after growth forecasts slumped to 0.9%, while India (-USD122.2m) and Thailand (-USD188.4m) faced political and tariff pressures. Drivers? Rate cuts boosted Indonesia, but U.S. tariffs and slowing exports spooked others—investors are hedging bets amid uncertainty.
Malaysia Breakdown: Foreign Exodus Continues
Foreigners dumped Malaysian stocks for the 7th straight week, with a net outflow of -RM314.4m! They sold every day except Friday (a small RM177.2m bounce). Meanwhile, local institutions snapped up bargains—buying for the 4th week (+RM391.8m). But retail investors joined the sell-off, exiting for the 2nd week (-RM77.3m). Trading volumes heated up: average daily volume rose sharply, with foreign activity up 10.0% and institutions surging 14.5%.
Stock Spotlight: Who's Buying What?
Foreigners' Top Picks
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ RM208.6m
$SUNWAY (5211.MY)$ RM112.8m
$SDG (5285.MY)$ RM70.2m
Retailers' Top Picks
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ RM47.1m
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ RM23.2m
$ZETRIX (0138.MY)$ RM21.4m
Strategy Breakdown: Clash of the Titans!
Local Institutions: Betting big on banks and utilities for long-term value—think defensive plays amid policy shifts. They're hoarding cash cows like $CIMB (1023.MY)$, ignoring short-term noise.
Local Retail: Chasing consumer and tech darlings like $ZETRIX (0138.MY)$—signaling short-term speculation! But they dumped industrials on tariff fears.
Foreign Players: Selling telecoms aggressively while nibbling banks—global risk aversion rules. Why the mismatch? Institutions have deeper pockets for bargains, while retail rides hype. Foreign cash is flighty—tariffs and growth doubts make them skittish!
Risks to Watch
Trade Wars: More U.S. tariffs could hammer Malaysia's electronics and palm oil exports.
Ringgit Risk: USD surged +0.32%to RM4.2267– a drag on foreign returns.
Domestic Inflation: July's +1.2% CPI(insurance costs up +5.5%) may squeeze consumer spending.

body: The outlook for Genting over the next three months appears cautiously optimistic, while also accompanied by certain risks that warrant attention. Core Business Outlook In the coming three months, Genting's core business drivers are expected to primarily stem from its leisure and hospitality segment, which contributes over 80% of the group's revenue. The ongoing recovery of the global tourism industry, particularly the enhanced airline connectivity in the Asia-Pacific region and the relaxation of visa policies (such as the easing of visa restrictions between China and Singapore), will continue to drive visitor traffic to Resorts World Genting (RWG) and Resorts World Sentosa (RWS). Notably, Genting Singapore intends to construct an integrated resort in the UAE, which could also serve as a potential catalyst for market sentiment. The plantation business benefits from stable palm oil prices and increased production, and is expected to maintain strong performance, providing support to the group's overall results. The power sector may also remain robust against the backdrop of rising demand in Asia, but attention should be paid to the long-term impacts of the transition to renewable energy. Financial Forecast and Valuation Financial Metrics Recent Performance/Forecast Data Source Q2 2024 Net Profit MYR 239.6 million (an increase of 49% year-on-year) Q2 2024 Revenue MYR 6.86 billion (an increase of 3% year-on-year) Earnings Per Share (2024E) estimated at approximately MYR 0.44 TTM Price-to-Earnings Ratio approximately 12.98 times Recent Stock Price Performance increased by 5.61% since the beginning of 2024 (during the same period, the Bursa Malaysia Index increased by 11.05%) Dividend Yield TTM approximately 3.13% Despite Genting's significant growth in net profit for the second quarter of 2024, it is important to note that some analysts have revised down their dividend expectations for Genting over the next three years, considering factors such as its subsidiary Genting Malaysia retaining capital for investments. This suggests that future dividend payouts may be under pressure. Potential Investment Risks Investing in Genting also requires attention to the following risks: 1. Exchange Rate and Geopolitical Risks: Genting operates across multiple countries, and its performance is susceptible to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates (particularly the USD/MYR exchange rate) and global geopolitical conflicts. 2. Legal and Regulatory Risks: Although lawsuits in the United States have largely concluded, the group still faces other legal challenges (such as the Bahamas case). Any adverse rulings could lead to financial and reputational losses. 3. Market Competition and Cost Pressures: The leisure and gaming industry is highly competitive. Additionally, rising operating costs, interest expenses, and depreciation costs may compress profit margins. 4. Seasonal Fluctuations: The fourth quarter is traditionally a low season for the leisure tourism industry, during which there have historically been significant performance declines. Attention should be paid to the potential recurrence of such seasonal fluctuations over the next three months. Key Focus Points for the Next Three Months In the next three months, the following aspects can be closely monitored: · Recovery trend of tourism: Focus on the number of tourists in Malaysia, Singapore, and the United States, particularly the recovery of Chinese tourists, which directly impacts the revenue of Genting's core business. · Progress of important projects: Monitor the upgrade progress of Genting Singapore's RWS 2.0, the effectiveness of the 60th anniversary celebration activities, as well as the advancement of new projects in the plantation and oil and gas sectors (such as the FLNG facility in the Kasuri block in Indonesia). · Updates on financial statements: Pay attention to the next quarterly report regarding revenue growth, adjusted EBITDA margins, and cash flow status. · Analyst opinions and market sentiment: Track whether analytical agencies have new ratings or target price adjustment reports. Investment Recommendation Overall, Genting is in a phase of both recovery and challenges over the next three months. · For short-term investors, the stock price's response to favorable factors for tourism recovery, changes in market sentiment, and technical levels may be the focus. However, caution should be exercised regarding seasonal off-peak periods and potential market volatility risks. For long-term investors, Genting's diversified business structure (including leisure, agriculture, and power) provides a certain degree of risk resilience. Although the current valuation lags behind the market index, it does not seem to fully reflect all of its recovery potential and asset value (such as the potential of its pharmaceutical company TauRx, which is underestimated by the market). Long-term investments should pay more attention to the ongoing recovery of its various business segments, the return on investment for new projects, and the group's overall debt management and cash flow generation capabilities. Please note: Stock market information changes rapidly, and the content of this article is an analysis and interpretation based solely on currently available public information and does not constitute any investment advice. Before making any investment decisions, please be sure to conduct independent judgment, in-depth research, and consult with a professional financial advisor. I hope the above analysis can provide you with a reference.

author: Moomoo Buddy
body:
Hi There!

It may be due to the stock prices adjustment.

Stock prices adjustment is the restoration of the stock price by charting the price movement according to the actual ups and downs of the stock and adjusting the trading volume to the same equity caliber. After a stock has undergoes ex-rights or ex-dividend, the stock price then changes.

No adjustment (Actual): When a listed company has a corporate action (like dividend payment or split/reverse split), a certain difference in stock price will show between before and after the ex-rights date. In reality, there is no significant change in stock value before and after the ex-date. However, when this price change reflects in the technical indicators, it may affect the accuracy of the indicators and the judgment of some investors.

Adjust forward (Default): Adjust the pre-ex-rights data based on the price point on the first day after the ex-date.

Adjust backward: Adjust the ex-rights data based on the price point on the last day before the ex-date.

Possible scenarios: Take Tencent (00700.HK). The lowest price adjusted forward is negative, and the current price adjusted backward is well above the current traded market price.

The Gig Workers Bill 2025 was passed by Parliament on Thursday. It is expected to benefit 1.2 million gig economy workers in Malaysia by recognizing them as a distinct category of the workforce and providing them with legal protections through written agreements.
The market expects Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) to cut interest rates in the coming months, but economists foresee rates remaining stable. BNM's recent 0.25% rate cut, its first since 2020, may be the last for now, supported by a strong economy and favorable US tariff rates.

title: I have great confidence in Genting.
body:
His fundamental range is approximately RM3. If the group's 'underlying value' is considered to be stable business + existing asset value (Genting Malaysia + Genting Singapore + Energy + Plantations), then the stock price in the RM3–3.3 range can be understood as the 'asset value floor.' I believe it is currently only undervalued; as long as you purchase below 3, it is essentially a guaranteed profit.
In a favorable scenario (U.S. license approval + improvement in investor sentiment): RM4.00 is reasonable. As for if the U.S. operations successfully materialize + profits rebound, then RM5.00–6.00 could be possible. However, I do not recommend betting on this, as the risks are too high.
Finance and Dividends The lack of dividend distribution may continue, as the company requires funds to support expansion and debt. Long-term investors lack return attractiveness → Insufficient support for stock prices. Business Outlook Increased Regulation of the Gaming Industry: Uncertainty Surrounds License Applications in the U.S.; if unsuccessful, it could jeopardize the most significant growth narrative. Reliance on a Single Industry: The casino's revenue share is excessively high and is significantly influenced by economic and policy cycles. Global Economic Instability: A decrease in tourists would directly impact the business of resorts and casinos. Stock Price Trend Fundamental Range: Hovering between RM2.8 and RM3.2 Further decline: If the U.S. license fails and the economy slows down, the stock price may drop to RM2.5. However, it is unlikely to be that severe; RM3.0 should still hold.
Summary: Genting may fall into a situation of 'high investment, low return' in the coming years. Without stable dividends, business expansion comes with high risks, lacking the appeal for long-term capital. → Not suitable for conservative investors; it is more of a high-risk speculative stock. If you are looking to earn dividends, Genting is definitely not the best choice.
It is merely a personal opinion.

title: Asian Capital Flees as Fed Rate Cut Looms: Who's Holding the Fort in Malaysia?
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Fed cuts are coming – and global markets are bracing! With the Fed set to blink in September, tariffs and shaky growth have investors on edge. Asia's funds fled last week, and Malaysia experienced significant market movements. Here's your quick take on where the money's moving and what it means for your portfolio.
Market Pulse
Last week, global markets felt the heat from U.S. tariffs and signals from the Fed. The U.S. economy grew a solid 3.3% in Q2, driven by business investment, but consumer spending slowed to just 1.6%. Why? Rising tariffs squeezed households. Inflation held at 2.5%, and job growth slumped to 35,000 per month—signaling trouble. The Fed's likely to cut rates in September to ease pressure. Most global indices dropped, with 13 out of 20 in the red. China's Shenzhen CSI 300 led gains (+2.71%), while France's CAC40 plunged (-3.34%).
Asia's Money Moves: India Leads Exodus, Indonesia Defies Trend
Foreign cash fled Asia big time! Total net outflows hit -USD3.34 billion, marking two straight weeks of selling. India bled the most (-USD1.48 billion), followed by South Korea (-USD697 million) and Thailand (-USD383 million). Only Indonesia saw inflows (USD92 million), thanks to tariff exemptions on exports. Why the exodus? U.S. tariffs spooked investors, while India's strong 7.8% GDP growth and Japan-India defense deals weren't enough to stem the tide. Risk aversion is rising fast across the region!
Malaysia Breakdown: Foreigners Flee, Locals Fight Back
Malaysia's market felt the heat: foreigners dumped stocks for the 8th week straight, yanking out RM1.41 billion (that's 4.47x higher than the week before. But locals fought back: institutions scooped up RM1.16 billion for their 5th buying week, and retailers jumped in too with RM249.4 million after two weeks of selling. Trading got busier – average daily volume surged: foreign activity spiked 76.4%, institutions 13.3%, and retailers 14.9%. Sectors? Foreigners loved Transport (RM44.5m inflow) but hated Financials (RM752.6m outflow). Tough week, but local support held firm!
Stock Spotlight: Who's Buying What?
Foreigners' Top Picks
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ RM171.7m
$SUNWAY (5211.MY)$ RM127.7m
$KGB (0151.MY)$ RM64.1m
Retailers' Top Picks
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ RM67.5m
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ RM57.7m
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ RM51.3m
Strategy Breakdown: Who's Playing What Game?
Local institutions are all about stability – they're loading up on banks and healthcare for long-term value, betting on policy support like Malaysia's upgraded growth forecast. Defensive moves!
Local retailers? They're chasing short-term thrills – think consumer favorites like $MRDIY (5296.MY)$ or gaming stocks. Hot money tactics, but easily spooked by news.
Foreigners are bailing globally: dumping banks for safety amid Fed uncertainty and tariff risks. They're hedging against currency swings and slowdowns.
Why the clash? Institutions have deep pockets for the long haul, retailers ride waves, and foreigners flee at the first sign of trouble. Information gaps and risk appetites drive the divide!
Risks to Watch
Stay alert: Fed rate cuts could spark more volatility.
Political risks: Indonesia's protests rattled markets.
Tariff wars threaten exports: Malaysia's PPI deflation shows pressure.
Don't forget inflation: Malaysia's CPI is creeping up.

title: Looking at 1,605 points in terms of the overall index target, Malaysian stocks led the five major investment themes in the final quarter
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Based on the overall index target, 1605 points Top 5 investment themes for Malaysian stocks in the final quarter
Following the fiscal year 2025 results season, CIMB raised the ratings of some Sector. At the same time, it believes that with improved domestic liquidity, lower interest rates, and a relatively stable political environment, the investment opportunities for Malaysian stocks at the end of the second half of the year can be summarized into five core themes. Currently, analysts have raised the rating of the Malaysian Planting Industry from “neutral” to “increase holdings.” The main reasons include SD dental straightening $SDG (5285.MY)$In the first half of the year, it surpassed expectations, improved palm oil price prospects, and cooperated with Financial Services $GAMUDA (5398.MY)$Jointly develop solar energy projects and strengthen their renewable energy layout. Analysts also maintain an “bullish” stance on building materials, construction, Medical, telecommunications, and utilities. ==== The five core investment themes for Malaysian stocks in the final quarter: ●Theme 1: Resilience in domestic demand In the second half of this year, the government's one-time payment of RM100 Mercy Basic Assistance Fund (SARA) became a key support. This amount of Cash/Money Market was distributed from August 31 to December 31, bringing the total amount of SARA and Mercy Assistance Fund (STR) for the whole year to RM15 billion. Direct funding to low- and middle-income cohort is expected to translate into stronger consumption of daily necessities. Looking ahead, with the straightening of the RON95 RBOB Gasoline subsidy, the government is likely to submit the 2026 budget in October to further strengthen SARA efforts to hedge against rising oil prices, thus continuing consumption momentum. In terms of beneficiary stocks, 99 Speed Mart $99SMART (5326.MY)$It is regarded as the most direct beneficiary due to its nationwide network of stores. AEON $AEON (6599.MY)$with Mr.diy $MRDIY (5296.MY)$, it is expected to benefit from weak consumption and demand for daily necessities, while Farm Fresh$FFB (5306.MY)$With a wide range of retail channels and new product launches, it is also possible to lock in necessary consumption growth. ●Theme 2:2026 Malaysian Tourism Year 2026 will be an important milestone for the Malaysian tourism industry. The government has set an ambitious target of 35.6 million visitors and RM147.1 billion in tourism revenue. The strategy focuses on creating demand, increasing passenger flow, and targeting the target market. This will directly benefit the leisure, retail and medical tourism sectors. Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$With Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$It is expected to welcome more gamblers and visitors, and theme parks will be the center of traffic. Sunway $SUNWAY (5211.MY)$With Sunway $SUNREIT (5176.MY)$With the advantage of integrating retail malls, hotels and leisure facilities, it is expected to amplify travel dividends. In terms of medical tourism sector, Johor Healthcare $KPJ (5878.MY)$with IHH Medical Group $IHH (5225.MY)$They were also named potential winners. ●Theme 3: Infrastructure and Industrialization Malaysia's medium-term economic growth path is being supported by multiple policy frameworks, such as the Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), the Rouxin Special XINJINGJI Zone, the New Industry Blueprint (NIMP 2030), and the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP). These plans are aimed at speeding up industrialization, increasing economic complexity, and strengthening the country's competitiveness. Construction and infrastructure units, including Financial Services University and IJM $IJM (3336.MY)$It will directly benefit from large-scale projects and transportation links. Utilities and energy, there is National Energy $TENAGA (5347.MY)$, Yang Zhongli Electric Power $YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$Demand for electricity is expected to grow due to industrialization, investment in data centers and renewable energy. Logistics and ports, including Westport Holdings $WPRTS (5246.MY)$, with a view to benefiting from the integration of industrial corridors and supply chains. Industry and industrial development, including SD Yajili and Ma Xing Group $MAHSING (8583.MY)$, Sunway, UEM Sunshine$UEMS (5148.MY)$It has the advantage of meeting the needs of industrial parks and comprehensive development. The banking sector, on the other hand, is an indirect beneficiary. Because of its participation in financing and structural design, it can benefit from the multiplier effect. ●Topic 4: Defensive Dividend Strategy In a volatile environment, high dividends have become investors' preferred defensive strategy. The overall dividend ratio of Malaysian stocks reached 4.2%, higher than Indonesia (3.8%), Thailand (4.0%), and only lower than Singapore (4.8%). The banking sector is seen as a sound choice, including Public Bank $PBBANK (1295.MY)$, Hong Leong Bank $HLBANK (5819.MY)$, Societe Generale Bank $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$Bank of India $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$The dividend ratio ranges from 5% to 6%. Telecom stocks such as Tiandi Tong Digital Network $CDB (6947.MY)$, Malaysia Telecom $TM (4863.MY)$, Mingxun $MAXIS (6012.MY)$Cash/Money Market flow is stable, and dividend rate is around 5%. In the planting industry, Daan $TAANN (5012.MY)$It is particularly prominent, with a dividend rate of up to 8%, backed by a net Cash/Money Market balance sheet and a strong dividend policy. Overall, these stocks form a steady “dividend basket”, providing stable returns and Cash/Money Market flow guarantees for defensive investors. ●Theme 5: Return of value Some stocks have been at low valuations for many years due to industry headwinds or short-term profit pressure, but they have strong fundamentals and opportunities for revaluation. Bumi Amada $ARMADA (5210.MY)$Currently, the stock price is only 4 times the capital to profit ratio in fiscal year 2025, 0.3 times the face value of the stock price. The order book reached RM19.8 billion, and the net debt ratio was 21.8%. High-yield product industry $KOSSAN (7153.MY)$The stock price was discounted by 25% against the book value, holding RM1.7 billion in net Cash/Money Market, accounting for 53% of the Market Cap. Net profit is expected to pick up as demand for gloves stabilizes and sales prices bottom out. Horse Resources $MRCB (1651.MY)$The partial valuation was discounted by 72%, and the stock price was only half of the book value. Yongan Group $YOCB (5159.MY)$The 2026 capital-to-profit ratio was only 7.5 times, with a net Cash/Money Market of 0.1 billion 46 million ringgit, accounting for 55% of the Market Cap, and a dividend ratio of 5.3% to 6.2%. These undervalued stocks are all seen as attractive risk-return combinations. ===== Subtext: Raising the Composite Index outlook Analysts pointed out that although net profit performance for the second quarter was moderate, with only 16% of companies exceeding expectations and 29% losing, management guidance for the second half of the year was optimistic, and 20% of companies announced higher dividends. Currently, analysts have lowered the forecast for core net profit growth of the Composite Index for FY2025 from 3.4% to 0.9%, while maintaining 7.5% growth in 2026. However, based on political stability, improved domestic liquidity, and interest rate cuts by the Bank of China, analysts raised the target for the end of 2025 from 1,560 points to 1,605 points, corresponding to 15.3 times the price-earnings ratio. Overall, short-term risks such as the appreciation of the ringgit to suppress overseas revenue, the imposition of tariffs on Malaysia by the US, and the expansion of sales and service taxes have been broadly reflected in the valuation, and the market is expected to usher in a phased revaluation.

title: Foreign Funds Net Outflow from CIMB RM367.4M as Local Retail Leans Towards PBBANK
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Markets climbed globally last week, fueled by signs of a cooling labor market—but beneath the surface, money moved in surprising ways. Let's dive in!
Market Pulse
Global markets saw mixed action amid key economic shifts! U.S. unemployment jumped to 4.3% in August, hitting a near-four-year high, while nonfarm payrolls added just 22K jobs—way below forecasts. This sparked bets on slower Fed rate hikes, nudging stocks like Nasdaq (+1.14%) higher.
Europe's PMI inched up to 51.0, signaling modest growth, but inflation crept to 2.1%, keeping ECB rates steady. China's factory PMI contracted for a fifth straight month, while the services gauge rebounded.
Oil prices dropped -3.85%, while palm oil rose +1.55%, showing commodity jitters. Overall, investors turned cautiously optimistic, chasing growth but eyeing risks.
Asia's Money Moves
Asia saw a net inflow of USD440m last week, breaking a two-week sell-off streak!
South Korea led with USD578m in buys, driven by tariff exemptions on tech exports and policy stability. Thailand flipped to a small USD22m inflow as budget passage eased political fears. But India bled -USD1.39b—its eighth straight outflow—due to U.S. tariffs and inflation worries. Indonesia lost -USD254m amid protests and new tariffs, while Vietnam extended outflows to seven weeks.
Why the shift? Tariff tensions and domestic unrest spooked investors, but policy support in stronger markets drew cash back.
Malaysia Breakdown
Foreign investors dumped Malaysian stocks for the ninth week straight, with a net outflow of RM187.6m—but it’s way smaller than last week's RM1.41b exit!
Shortened holidays (markets closed Monday and Friday) dampened activity. Locals stepped up: institutions bought for the sixth week (RM148.6m net), and retail investors joined in for a second week (RM38.9m net).
Daily trading volume plunged across the board: foreign ADTV crashed -42.2%, retail fell -15.7%, and institutions dropped -17.5%.
What’s the take? Foreigners fled, but locals held firm—showing resilience amid thin trading.
Stock Spotlight: Who’s Buying What?
Investors showed clear favorites and flops last week—here’s the lowdown!
Foreign Investors' Top Sells:
$CIMB (1023.MY)$ (Financials, -RM367.4m)
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ (Financials, -RM126.7m)
$TENAGA (5347.MY)$ (Utilities, -RM61.8m)
Local Institutions' Top Buys:
$CIMB (1023.MY)$ (Financials, RM342.1m)
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ (Financials, RM70.7m)
$PPB (4065.MY)$ (Plantation, RM46.6m)
Local Retail's Favorites:
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ (Financials, RM28.5m)
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ (Consumer, RM20.3m)
$TENAGA (5347.MY)$ (Utilities, RM13.8m)
Strategy Breakdown: Why the Clash?
Investors aren't on the same page—here's why!
– Local Institutions: They're all about financials and utilities for long-term value. Snapping up banks like CIMB amid rate stability signals? That's classic defensive play, betting on steady dividends and policy support. But they dumped construction stocks—maybe profit-taking after recent gains?
– Local Retail: Chasing consumer and financial names—think Public Bank and Genting! This screams short-term speculation: jumping on household brands and dividend payers. Yet they ditched laggards like Genting Malaysia, showing quick exits when sentiment sours.
– Foreign Investors: Fleeing Malaysian financials big time! Selling CIMB and Public Bank hints at global risk-off—tariffs and weak growth spooked them. But they nibbled at construction and healthcare for potential growth. Why the split? Locals have home-ground info, while foreigners eye global volatility and FX risks (Ringgit dipped -0.10%)!
Risks to Watch
Stay alert—these could rock your portfolio! Policy uncertainty is key, like Malaysia’s budget debates and U.S. tariffs. Also, inflation risks loom—India's input costs surged, and Vietnam's prices jumped. Trade gaps widened globally, so watch for market swings. Investors, is your strategy ready for turbulence?

title: In the three trading days last week, foreign investors net sold 188 million Malaysian Ringgit in Malaysian stocks.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 8th) Foreign capital has fled the Malaysian stock market for the ninth consecutive week. Fortunately, due to only three trading days last week, the net foreign selling amounted to a 'mere' 187.6 million ringgit, significantly lower than the 1.41 billion ringgit recorded the previous week. According to the fund flow report from Maybank Investment Bank, foreign investors only net purchased Malaysian stocks worth 173.2 million ringgit last Wednesday; the largest net selling occurred on Tuesday, totaling 251.5 million ringgit, while Thursday recorded a net selling of 109.3 million ringgit. From a sector perspective, the three sectors that attracted the most foreign capital inflow last week were construction (135.3 million ringgit), transportation and logistics (41.5 million ringgit), and healthcare (38.9 million ringgit). The sectors with the highest capital flight of foreign investment are financial services (-417.1 million MYR), telecommunications and media (-43.1 million MYR), and utilities (-35.9 million MYR). The report also indicated that local institutions net purchased 148.6 million MYR worth of Malaysian stocks last week, marking six consecutive weeks of net buying; local retail investors also net bought Malaysian stocks for two consecutive weeks, with a net purchase of 38.9 million MYR last week. In addition, the average daily trading volume (ADTV) generally declined last week, with foreign investors, local institutions, and retail investors decreasing by 42.2%, 17.5%, and 15.7% respectively.
Top 10 stocks purchased the most by foreign investors: $GAMUDA (5398.MY)$ , $FFB (5306.MY)$ , $SUNCON (5263.MY)$ , $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ , $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ , $WPRTS (5246.MY)$ , $IOIPG (5249.MY)$ , $SIME (4197.MY)$ , $PETGAS (6033.MY)$ , $MCEMENT (3794.MY)$

title: PETRONAS retains its crown as Malaysia’s most valuable brand for the 15th consecutive year
author: yytan
body:
KUALA LUMPUR, 29 MAY 2025 – Malaysia’s top 100 brands grew by 16% in 2025, reaching a total brand value of USD59.1 billion, reflecting strong national economic performance, according to the latest Malaysia 100 2025 report by Brand Finance, the world’s leading brand valuation consultancy. Oil & gas and banking sector brands ranked this year accounted for 45% of the total brand value, led by PETRONAS and Maybank at the forefront . Leisure & tourism, ranked as the third most valuable sector in the rankings, is led by Genting amid increased tourism following visa-free policies. Nearly all industries saw double-digit growth , highlighting the resilience and adaptability of Malaysian brands in a fast-changing economic landscape. PETRONAS (brand value down 1% to USD14.4 billion) remains Malaysia’s most valuable brand for the 15th year, despite a slight decline due to lower oil prices and market volatility. Maybank (up 52% to USD5.2 billion) ranks second, driven by its M25+ strategy focusing on digital innovation and customer centricity, including the launch of its Money Lock feature. Genting (up 37% to USD4.9 billion) ranks third, boosted by strong tourism recovery, high-yield Chinese visitors, and enhanced digitalisation at Resorts World Genting. Proton (brand value up 30% to USD312 million) has emerged as Malaysia’s strongest brand ranked in 2025, with a Brand Strength Index (BSI) score of 93.9/100 and a AAA+ brand strength rating. This marks a major leap in public trust and appeal, thanks to popular models like the X50, the new S70 sedan, and its first EV, the e.MAS 7. Tenaga Nasional (up 35% to USD2.3 billion), follows in second place powered by strong forecasts and infrastructure growth, recording a BSI score of 88.9/ 100 and an AAA rating. Mr D.I.Y. (brand value up 15% to USD619 million) takes third place, scoring 87.8/100 for its BSI score supported by its rapid expansion and meaningful community efforts.
Meanwhile, Malaysia Airlines (brand value up 209% to USD607 million) is the fastest-growing Malaysian brand in 2025. The brand’s commendable brand value growth has elevated it to a top position domestically while also earning it the title of the fastest-growing airline brand globally as it re-entered the Brand Finance Airlines 50 2025 ranking after a 10-year absence. Its impressive turnaround is driven by fleet renewal through fuel-efficient aircraft, strategic route realignments, and digital investments. These efforts have boosted operational performance and resilience. With Asia Pacific air travel set to surge, Malaysia Airlines is poised to capitalise on international growth and reclaim its position as a leading global carrier.
Other highlights from the Brand Finance’s Malaysia 100 2025 report: MyEG (brand value up 119% to USD100 million) experienced a 29% increase in its BSI score to 80.9/100, the largest year-on-year growth among Malaysian brands ranked this year, making it a key player in its niche e-government commercial services sector. CIMB Group (brand value up 20% to USD2.5 billion) takes the fourth position followed by Sime Darby (brand value up 6% to USD2.3 billion) ranked as the fifth most valuable brand in Malaysia. AirAsia (brand value up 66% to USD1.9 billion) secured the seventh spot, with significant growth from strategic route expansions and high passenger load factors. Celcomdigi (brand value up 22% to USD1.7 billion), eighth most valuable brand in the ranking, saw strategic network modernisation and AI-driven innovation supporting its position as the most valuable Malaysian telecoms brand. author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 17th) As the Federal Reserve's interest rate cut is imminent, foreign capital has also ended a nine-week net selling streak, flowing back into Malaysian stocks with RM223.9 million, helping the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI surpass the 1600 level. According to the fund flow report by Maybank Investment Bank, foreign investors turned net buyers on three out of five trading days, with the largest net inflow occurring on Friday, amounting to MYR 230.7 million. This was followed by Thursday (MYR 107.1 million) and Tuesday (MYR 28 million). In terms of sectors, the three sectors that received the highest foreign net inflows last week were industrial products (MYR 132.1 million), plantations (MYR 93.9 million), and construction (MYR 92.8 million). Meanwhile, local institutions ended their six-week streak of net buying, turning into net sellers last week with an outflow of MYR 133 million. Local retail investors also switched from buying to selling, ending two consecutive weeks of net buying, recording net sales of MYR 90.9 million last week. Additionally, the average daily trading volume (ADTV) of all investor categories declined last week. Foreign investors experienced the largest drop, contracting by 18.9%, while local institutions and retail investors fell by 14.9% and 1.83%, respectively.

title: Good News in New York Casino Bid: Genting Reaches Final Selection, Decision by End of Year
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Cloud Top$GENTING (3182.MY)$ Good news has arrived for the bidding plan for casino licenses in Downstate New York, with two companies becoming the first to gain the support of local community advisory board votes, and their proposals will now proceed to the state government for final review. According to a Bloomberg report, Genting's $5.5 billion (approximately RM23.16 billion) Queens casino resort expansion plan and MGM Resorts International’s $2.3 billion (approximately RM9.69 billion) Empire City Casino expansion proposal have become the first two bids to receive voting support from New York’s local community advisory boards. Final Decision on December 1 The New York Gaming Facility Location Board will review the bids from Genting and MGM and make a final decision on December 1 this year. Since both proposals involve expansions of existing casinos and already have established engagement with local communities, they possess greater flexibility compared to entirely new casino developments and face less opposition. Genting, through its subsidiary Genting New York under Genting Malaysia (GENM, 4715, Main Market Consumer Stock), is participating in the multi-year casino license bidding process in Downstate New York. Genting plans to significantly expand its casino resort located next to the Aqueduct Racetrack, adding 2,000 hotel rooms, an arena, and more than 30 restaurants and bars. Creation of 5,000 Job Opportunities (Subtitle) Genting claims that the resort will create up to 5,000 permanent jobs. Genting, which already operates a casino in the Catskills, also stated that if the company wins the new casino license, the New York State government can begin generating revenue from the additional gaming tables and slot machines within six months. Genting stated that by 2027, the gambling revenue of the new casino is expected to more than double to USD 2.2 billion annually (approximately MYR 9.26 billion). Regarding support for local communities, Robert DeSalvio, President of Genting Americas East, stated: 'This support and vote demonstrate the mission we have consistently upheld over the past 15 years—to be the best neighbor in Queens.' The New York State government plans to issue up to three new casino licenses in this round of bidding. Three Other Proposals Under Evaluation Bloomberg reported that last week, three proposals to build casinos in Manhattan were rejected by local communities. These plans were proposed by SL Green Realty, Silverstein Properties, and the Soloviev Group, respectively. In addition, three other bidding proposals are awaiting evaluation by the Community Advisory Committee, including Bally's project in the Bronx, a project in Coney Island, and a proposal by Steve Cohen, owner of the New York Mets, for a casino at Citi Field in Queens. In any case, the Coney Island project faces widespread opposition from local legislators and has a lower chance of passing through a vote.

title: Why LVS, WYNN & MGM dropped and how this benefit GENTING
body: 🧩 Context: Why LVS, WYNN & MGM dropped and how this benefit GENTING The sell-off on Friday wasn’t because the global casino industry is collapsing — it was Macau-specific and sentiment-driven: • Weak Golden Week travel numbers from China → lower Macau gaming expectations. • Weather disruption / storm risk → short-term revenue hit. • Investor risk rotation out of “China exposure.” So, the issue is mostly Macau and Chinese tourism, not the U.S. or ASEAN casino market. 💡 Short-Term Effects (Next Few Weeks) ✅ Investor Rotation Benefit • U.S. and ASEAN investors may rotate out of Macau-heavy stocks (LVS, WYNN, MGM) into non-Macau operators like Genting Singapore and Genting Malaysia. • Fund managers seeking exposure to gaming recovery but wanting to avoid China risk will find Genting relatively safer. ✅ RWLV (Las Vegas) • RWLV could actually benefit from this shift • U.S. leisure spending remains resilient. • Las Vegas strip demand stable → U.S. gaming earnings viewed as “safe cash flow.” • Some funds that trim LVS, MGM positions could rotate part of that capital into RWLV’s parent exposure via Genting Berhad. ✅ Valuation Multiple Gap May Narrow • Genting stocks have been trading at a “conglomerate discount” • If Macau sentiment stays weak, Genting’s diversified earnings become more attractive → valuation uplift potential. 🔮 4️⃣ Medium-Term Effects (2–6 Months) • RWNY & NY Casino License Story Strengthens: • With MGM distracted by weak Macau sentiment, Genting’s RWNY license narrative becomes even more strategic — investors see it as growth anchored in the U.S., not in China. • This can support Genting Berhad and GENM share price ahead of the license decision. • GENS (Singapore) Stability Premium: • Singapore tourism continues to recover steadily from ASEAN and India, not just China. • GENS often rallies when Macau weakens because it captures “safe Asia gaming” flows. ⚖️ 5️⃣ Net Impact Summary Time Horizon Genting Berhad Genting Malaysia Genting Singapore Short Term (1–3 weeks) Slight upside from rotation Stable, potential upside Likely outperform regionally Medium Term (3–6 months) Moderate upside if NY license news improves Strong upside (Empire Resort story) Defensive outperformance. US Assets consolidation and listing separately in NYSE? 🧭 In summary: • LVS, WYNN & MGM declines are negative for Macau sentiment, but positive for Genting’s relative positioning. • Genting’s U.S. and Singapore diversification now look more valuable. • Expect fund inflows and a potential relative outperformance window over the next 48 weeks.

Good morning mooers! Here are things you need to know about today's market:
U.S. Stocks Rally as Trade Tensions Ease; Gold and Silver Hit Record Highs
Malaysian Stocks Dip Amid Renewed US-China Trade Tensions
Malaysia Expands Tech Partnerships, Aims to Diversify Global Trade Relations
Stocks to watch: Genting, GenM, etc.
- Moomoo News MY
Wall Street Summary
$S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 6,654.72（+1.56%)
$Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ 46,067.58 (+1.29%)
$Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 22,694.61 (+2.21%)
Wall Street rebounded strongly on Monday, with the Nasdaq Composite jumping 2.2%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones gained over 1% each. The rally came as US-China trade tensions, which sparked Friday's sell-off, appeared to subside following President Trump's softer stance over the weekend.
Meanwhile, gold and silver prices soared to record highs amid the ongoing US government shutdown and expectations of potential Federal Reserve rate cuts. Gold futures reached $4,137.20 per ounce, while silver hit $50.625. In tech news, $Broadcom (AVGO.US)$ shares surged 9.9% after announcing a partnership with OpenAI to develop AI accelerators, though it remains unclear if this is related to the previously disclosed $10 billion customer agreement.
Bursa Market Insight
$FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ 1622.250 (-0.46%)
Top Gainer: $MISC (3816.MY)$ RM7.40 (+1.37%)
Top Loser: $MRDIY (5296.MY)$ RM1.66 (-2.35%)
USD/MYR: $USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.2228(-0.05%)
Bursa Malaysia closed lower on Monday, mirroring regional market declines as US-China trade concerns resurfaced. The FBM KLCI fell 0.43% to 1,615.19 points, with decliners outnumbering gainers by more than two to one.
Market sentiment soured after US President Donald Trump announced plans for new tariffs on Chinese exports, responding to China's recent restrictions on critical mineral exports. The broader market saw increased trading volume, with 3.57 billion shares changing hands, valued at RM2.82 billion.
Malaysia is taking steps to broaden its international trade and technology collaborations, with plans to sign a semiconductor agreement with Brazil and initiate tech-focused talks with India. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Liew Chin Tong announced these initiatives as part of the country's strategy to strengthen ties with developing economies, particularly BRICS nations and African countries.
The government is also prioritizing the reinforcement of regional supply chains, especially in the semiconductor sector, to enhance Malaysia's economic resilience. Additionally, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to visit Africa in November to further expand economic engagements, as Malaysia seeks to reduce its dependence on traditional markets like the United States.
IPO Scanner

$GENTING (3182.MY)$ has proposed a takeover bid to privatize $GENM (4715.MY)$, offering to acquire the remaining 50.64% stake for RM6.74 billion.

$OMESTI (9008.MY)$'s subsidiary has secured a contract from the Ministry of Home Affairs.
$MALAKOF (5264.MY)$ has signed an agreement with Mitsubishi Power Ltd for gas turbines and generators for a planned power plant in southern Peninsular Malaysia.
$SASBADI (5252.MY)$ has won a contract from the Ministry of Education to provide English language proficiency testing services.
$CLOUDPT (0277.MY)$ has upgraded to Bursa Malaysia's Main Market and is expanding its service offerings.

title: Genting's full acquisition offer lacks attractiveness; Genting Malaysia is worth up to MYR 3.28 per share.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Genting’s Full Acquisition Offer Lacks Appeal Genting Malaysia's Maximum Valuation Reaches RM3.28 per Share Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ Offering RM2.35 per share, fully acquiring and privatizing Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ The plan has sparked heated market discussions, with analysts holding divergent views. Some investment banks believe that the aforementioned offer does not take into account three major future benefits for Genting Malaysia, and its share price could potentially rise to MYR 3.28 at most. Genting needs to significantly increase its offer price to be fair; hence, shareholders are advised to reject the offer. Maybank Investment Bank analysts pointed out that although the offer price of MYR 2.35 per share is 21% higher than his previous target price of MYR 1.95 for Genting Malaysia, and 10% higher than yesterday's closing price of MYR 2.14, he believes that this offer does not truly reflect the value of Genting Malaysia. "Genting Malaysia has three potential benefits that may significantly increase its fair share price in the future, which are not reflected in the offer price of MYR 2.35 per share." First, the analyst stated that the value of the land in Miami acquired by Genting Malaysia in 2022 is expected to surge after revaluation. "Currently, we value the land based on the acquisition cost of USD 422 million (approximately MYR 1.78 billion). However, in 2023, Genting Malaysia planned to sell the land for USD 1.2 billion (approximately MYR 5.07 billion). Assuming the value of the land is reassessed at USD 1.2 billion, our fair price for the stock would increase by MYR 0.55 per share." Secondly, he noted that Empire Resort, a subsidiary of Genting Malaysia, might sell its non-gaming assets to Sullivan County's local development authority for resort facilities, which would add MYR 0.30 to its fair share price. Finally, the analyst pointed out that Genting Malaysia has a good chance of winning the casino license in New York's lower state, adding at least an additional MYR 0.48 to its fair valuation. "Therefore, under the best scenario, the fair price for Genting Malaysia could reach as high as MYR 3.28 per share. We believe that shareholders of Genting Malaysia should not accept this offer." Currently, the analyst has raised the target price for Genting Malaysia from the previous MYR 1.95 to MYR 2.97, and upgraded the rating from 'Hold' to 'Buy'."
Little chance of a price increase in the purchase offer. Additionally, analysts from DA Securities agree that Genting's full takeover offer lacks attractiveness. However, they believe it is unlikely that Genting will raise its bid. The likelihood of Genting raising its offer is low, as the board of Genting Malaysia has no need to seek additional competitive acquisition proposals. Therefore, this offer may not receive sufficient support, and Genting Malaysia may ultimately fail to be privatized and delisted. He added that, for Genting, privatizing Genting Malaysia is not necessarily the best option. We believe that privatizing Genting Malaysia is not a good idea because the securities market is crucial for its future financing activities, especially if Genting Malaysia wins the New York downstate casino license and plans to allocate USD 5.5 billion (approximately MYR 23.23 billion) for development. The analyst also recommended shareholders reject Genting’s offer.
Galaxy International: A good exit opportunity However, analysts at Galaxy International Securities hold a different view, suggesting that shareholders should accept the offer since Genting's bid is higher than their target price of MYR 1.88, providing shareholders with a decent exit opportunity. Moreover, should Genting Malaysia win the New York downstate casino license, it will need to allocate more working capital and capital expenditures, leading to a decline in earnings growth and reduced dividend payouts. In any case, he noted that many shareholders who have invested in Genting Malaysia might still be facing paper losses. Furthermore, given that the offer price reflects less than a 10% premium over the current share price, it may not garner enough shareholder support, resulting in the privatization attempt failing. Investors may also wait for the results of New York State’s casino license decision, which is expected to be announced on December 1st this year. Genting Malaysia once surged by 10% Shares of Genting Malaysia, which received a voluntary general offer from its parent company, surged as much as 10% at the opening today, reaching RM2.36, even surpassing the offer price of RM2.35 per share. As for Genting, as the acquiring party, its share price rose by up to 7% this morning, reaching RM3.06. Yesterday, major shareholder Genting issued a conditional voluntary general offer to acquire all remaining shares of Genting Malaysia at RM2.35 per share, or a total consideration of RM6.744 billion, followed by plans to privatize and delist the company. Currently, Genting holds 2,797,701,859 shares of Genting Malaysia, equivalent to 49.36% of the equity interest. Genting now plans to acquire the remaining 2,870,039,874 shares, representing 50.64% of the equity, with the transaction expected to be completed by the end of the fourth quarter of 2025.
Most investors bought at higher levels
Some investment banks believe that Genting's offer of RM2.35 per share for the full acquisition and privatization of Genting Malaysia may be difficult to materialize, but it could further increase its stake.
Analysts at Galaxy International Securities noted that the above offer should increase Genting’s stake in Genting Malaysia to over 49.4%, but the privatization plan is likely to fail, given that many shareholders who have invested in Genting Malaysia are still in a loss-making position on paper.
Most shareholders of Genting Malaysia may still face book losses, as the offer price of 2.35 ringgit remains below the stock's trading range of 2.50 to 3 ringgit between 2022 and 2024.
However, the analyst stated that if the privatization is successful, he will remove the 30% parent company stake discount applied in valuing Genting, implying a significant increase in Genting's target price at that time.
Genting's valuation is considered undervalued, as its 53% stake in Genting Singapore is currently valued 26% lower in Genting's books compared to Genting Singapore's market capitalization.
For now, he maintains a 'Buy' rating on Genting with a target price of 3.57 ringgit.
Genting's Earnings Expected to Surge by 51%
Additionally, an analyst from Maybank Investment Bank noted that privatizing Genting Malaysia could bring approximately 6.3 billion ringgit in new debt to Genting, which would initially offset additional earnings contributed by fully consolidating Genting Malaysia. However, in the long term, it presents significant upside potential for Genting.
The revaluation of land in Miami, potential divestment plans for non-gaming assets of Empire Resorts, and the possibility of securing a casino license in New York's Lower Hudson Valley are all major potential catalysts brought by Genting Malaysia.
If the privatization succeeds, the analyst said that Genting’s earnings could surge by 51% or more, with fair value per share potentially rising to 4.25 ringgit.
Currently, the analyst has maintained Genting's 'Buy' rating while raising its target price from 3.70 ringgit to 3.94 ringgit.

title: Titan Trading Notes For Wednesday [15/10/2025]:
author: Titan Capital
body:
fell back towards the 1611 points region with an overall negative market sentiment as we saw over 800 counters closing red for the day. Daily trading volume remains average around the 3.6 billion mark, dominated by sellers.
Main stocks that showed strong buying momentum would be the likes of GENM, TANCO, GENTING, SCIB, CHEEDING, MCLEAN, ECOSHOP, MRDIY, AXREIT, and 99SMART. All of which were able to sustain their rallies throughout the day on the top volumes list.
$GENM(4715.MY)$ following $GENTING(3182.MY)$ privatisation offer, gapped up in the morning and maintained around the RM 2.32 - RM 2.35 region as the offer from the buyer was RM 2.35.
Expecting for it to be trading within this range, as GENTING already holds almost 50% of GENM, the privatisation offer will likely go through in my opinion, so for those of you that are trapped from higher prices from before, may have to consider to take the loss and just move on.
Can monitor GENM closely to earn the difference if suddenly have some dips below RM 2.30 as offer to buy is RM 2.35.
I don't have much to say for the rest as I expect the market to be quite volatile and shaky in the coming weeks as the tug of war between US and China intensifies. Both will do what they can to pressure each other to come to their terms before making a deal.
Will be monitoring closely, and expect tech counters with high PE multiples to be the most vulnerable to suffer from profit taking activities.
Local consumer counters shouldn't be too affected by this, which is why we saw $MRDIY(5296.MY)$ , $99SMART(5326.MY)$ , and $ECOSHOP(5337.MY)$ perform quite well today.
Defensive counters like banking and plantation should also fare pretty well.
So monitor all of these closely before making any moves.

My explanation might not be very clear, but you can look into 'pyramid position building' to develop your own trading strategy. You can decide how many times you are comfortable adding to your position when buying in.
At the same time, avoid holding only one or two stocks in your account; diversify your investments to reduce the risk of making mistakes. Allocate no more than 5% of your portfolio to each stock, which gives you 20 chances to succeed compared to putting all your funds into a single stock where one mistake could lead to total loss.
Of course, there is also a strategy of always keeping 50% cash on hand. If a stock you believe in plummets for any reason but still has strong long-term fundamentals, and you find yourself without cash to buy at the bottom, wouldn’t that be quite embarrassing?

title: 🇲🇾 Titan Trading Notes For Thursday [16/10/2025]
author: Titan Capital
body:
closed pretty flat around the 1611 points region but the overall market sentiment definitely had a huge rebound today. Daily trading volume also surged back towards the 4.2 billion mark, so far a good signal here.
Main stocks that showed strong buying momentum would be the likes of VELESTO, GENTING, DNEX, TFP, CMSB, ECOSHOP, MRDIY, SCIB. NOVAMSC, 99SMART, SEDANIA, K1, SUPERMX, CHEEDING, HARTA, and DAYANG All of which were able to sustain their rallies throughout the day on the top volumes list.
$GENTING(3182.MY)$ was definitely one of the star performers today, breaking out huge all the way towards the RM 3.40+ regions with huge volume and buying momentum after its offer to take GENM private at RM 2.35 per share.
For now looking quite strong here and as long as able to hold above its RM3.20+ immediate support, could continue to breakout further towards the RM 3.50+ major resistance levels in the coming week.
Will be monitoring GENTING closely.
$DNEX(4456.MY)$ on the other hand also had a huge breakout all the way towards the RM 0.29+ regions with huge volume and buying momentum out of nowhere. This came after consolidating over the past few months without much action.
This breakout out of nowhere definitely caught my attention and if able to hold above its RM 0.275+ immediate support, could be breaking out towards and beyond its RM 0.33+ major resistance levels soon.
Will be monitoring DNEX closely
$CMSB(2852.MY)$ had a huge breakout today, rallying all the way from its RM 1.42 major resistance levels towards the RM 1.51 regions with massive volume and buying momentum.
Although it wasn't able to close on its intraday high, its closing price of RM 1.48 was still a pretty bullish signal and if able to keep this kind of buying momentum, could be trending up further towards the RM 1.50 - RM 1.70+ major resistance levels soon.
Will be monitoring CMSB closely.

title: See you at the summit.
author: 神机妙算（小军师）
body:
When I was in elementary school, I often scored 100% in math and moral education exams.
At that time, I was very young and thought that if everyone received 100%, I didn’t seem to be particularly special.
But there is no such thing as 101%. It was only when I grew up that I realized this.
It’s not that 101% doesn’t exist; it’s just that I was too young to understand back then.
It was my young age that constrained my way of thinking.
I am not speaking incoherently; it’s just that you need good results to prove yourself so others will pay attention to what you say.
Without achievements, everything is just empty talk. Isn’t society like that?

title: Lim Kok Thay has been aggressively purchasing shares at low prices and now controls over 50% of Genting Malaysia.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 17th report) Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ after launching a full takeover offer, has increased its stake in Genting Malaysia through open market purchases for two consecutive days at prices below the offer price of MYR 2.35, $GENM (4715.MY)$ with the current shareholding exceeding 50%.
According to the equity change announcement, Genting purchased a total of 36.1 million shares of Genting Malaysia on Tuesday (14th) and Wednesday (15th), increasing its stake from 49.36% to 50.02%.
The announcement disclosed that Genting made three separate purchases on Tuesday at MYR 2.31, MYR 2.32, and MYR 2.33 per share, acquiring 500,000 shares, 8 million shares, and 500,000 shares of Genting Malaysia in the open market, completing a total transaction of 9 million shares.
The following day, Genting completed the transaction of 27.1 million shares at a price of RM2.33 per share.
Genting announced on Monday (the 13th) that it would acquire the remaining shares it does not hold at RM2.35 per share or a total of RM6.7446 billion to advance the privatization process and delist from the stock exchange.
At that time, Genting held 49.36% of Genting Malaysia's equity.
Stimulated by the full acquisition announcement, Genting Malaysia's share price rose to RM2.36 upon resumption of trading on Tuesday, surpassing the offer price. However, in subsequent trading sessions, it mainly fluctuated between RM2.32 and RM2.34.
After announcing the full acquisition, Genting issued media announcements by noon the following day whenever there were trading activities concerning Genting Malaysia. However, as of 5:00 PM on Friday, no announcement regarding Thursday’s trades had been made.

title: The Must-Know Weekly Top Traded Stocks by Malaysians on Moomoo
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Last week, macro events drove market performance. Loan fraud cases disclosed by two US regional banks sparked concerns about the credit market. Combined with the ongoing US government shutdown and the recurring US-China trade conflict, panic spread, leading to a rush into safe-haven assets.$XAU/USD (XAUUSD.CFD)$ set a record high of $4,380 last week, with gold rising 6% on a weekly basis. The crypto market saw a decline, with $Bitcoin (BTC.CC)$ briefly falling below $104,000.
On Friday, Trump's moderate comments on US-China trade boosted a rebound in US stocks. The $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ finished the week up 1.70%, the $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ rose 2.14%, and the $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ gained 1.56%. Last week also marked the official start of the Q3 earnings season for US stocks, with major banks like $JPMorgan (JPM.US)$ and $Citigroup (C.US)$ reporting better-than-expected results. Attention this week will be on the earnings releases from tech stocks such as $Tesla (TSLA.US)$ .
Malaysia's economy demonstrated remarkable resilience, expanding by a surprising 5.2% in 25Q3, a figure that comfortably surpassed expectations. This robust growth, primarily fueled by strong domestic demand, a recovering tourism sector, and a rebound in mining output, has prompted several major research houses to revise their full-year economic forecasts upwards. Despite the improved immediate outlook, analysts express caution for 2026, pointing to potential external headwinds and the adverse effects of US trade tariffs on Malaysian exports. The $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ Index fell 0.93% last week to close at 1,607 points, as market volatility persisted.
US and Bursa stocks trading heat lists
Based on last week's trading data from moomoo MY, let's see which U.S. and Bursa stocks have seen a sustained increase in trading activity over the past week.
Nvidia launched the first Blackwell wafer produced in the US
$NVIDIA (NVDA.US)$ 's stock experienced minor weekly fluctuations. Last week, Nvidia launched the first Nvidia Blackwell wafer produced in the US, signaling that the Nvidia Blackwell AI chip is about to be mass-produced in the US and highlighting the core position of US domestic manufacturing in AI infrastructure.
After AMD announced a strategic cooperation with OpenAI, its $Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.US)$ Instinct series GPUs also received a large order from Oracle. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure will purchase the AMD Instinct MI450 series GPUs, with an initial plan to deploy 50,000 units starting in the third quarter of next year and plans to further expand in 2027 and beyond. AMD's stock rose 8.46% for the week. However, Oracle's stock fell 6.93% for the week, marking its worst single-day performance since January this year. After the market questioned the feasibility, there was a concentrated sell-off.
Despite reports that US memory chip giant Micron Technology plans to exit its data center server chip business in China, its stock still rose 11.44% for the week. The company will continue to supply two Chinese customers with significant data center operations outside of China.
Tesla's sales in China continue to grow
$Tesla (TSLA.US)$ 's stock rebounded 6.24% last week and announced its weekly sales in China. The company's steady growth in China is still ongoing. From October 6 to October 12, Tesla recorded 113,000 new insurance registrations in China, a figure that marks a 126% increase in sales compared to the previous week and also indicates a 33% year-over-year growth in the region compared to the same period last year. However, sales in Europe have declined. The market remains closely focused on Musk's trillion-dollar compensation plan. Tesla's Q3 FY2025 earnings, to be released after the market close on October 22, will be an important factor affecting its stock price movement.
The trading enthusiasm for the rare earth sector is gradually waning
Against the backdrop of China's rare earth export controls, the upward momentum of the rare earth sector after the surge is gradually declining. Some rare earth stocks in the US market have ended their consecutive upward trend. $MP Materials (MP.US)$ rose only 3.13% for the week, CRML rose 39.25%, and USAR fell 14.96%.
$Amazon (AMZN.US)$ is also one of the most actively traded individual stocks, but its stock has fallen for four consecutive weeks. Previously, Amazon announced the expansion of its pay-per-use telemedicine service platform, Amazon One Medical, allowing for pay-per-use access to treatment services for common childhood illnesses.
