Let's also take a look at which Bursa stocks were active over the past week.
Genting's Conditional Voluntary Takeover Offer
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ has launched a conditional voluntary takeover offer to acquire the remaining 50.64% stake in its subsidiary, Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ , for MYR 2.35 per share, valuing the deal at MYR 6.74 billion. The parent company aims to delist Genting Malaysia, which owns Resorts World Genting and Resorts World New York City. A key reason for the move is to better support Genting Malaysia's bid for a New York casino license, which involves a proposed US$5.5 billion integrated resort.
If successful, Genting Berhad believes its strengthened control will enhance the subsidiary's financial capacity for this major project. The offer represents a significant premium to recent share prices. Following the announcement, Nomura analysts upgraded Genting Malaysia to a "Buy" rating. Shares of Genting Berhad and GENM rose 17.83% and 9.35% last week.
99 Speed Mart on Strong Growth Outlook
99 Speed Mart $99SMART (5326.MY)$ Retail is the prime beneficiary of Malaysia's expanding government cash-aid. With its wide store network and appeal to price-sensitive consumers, it is well-positioned to capture demand from lower-income groups. Outlet expansion and its role as a major Nestle distributor are expected to sustain a 15% earnings growth. RHB raises the stock's target price to MYR3.56 from MYR2.81, maintaining a Buy rating.
Weekend stock events
Over the weekend, US President Trump met with Ukrainian President Zelensky and made statements on issues such as US supply of "Tomahawk" missiles to Ukraine. On interest rate cuts, Musalem of the Federal Reserve indicated that if employment faces more risks and inflation is under control, he may support the path of further interest rate cuts.
Meanwhile, after last week's continued gains, gold prices experienced selling pressure, with spot gold prices briefly falling below $4,200 per ounce.
Key stock events of this week
The coming week will be the earnings season, with companies such as $Netflix (NFLX.US)$ and $Tesla (TSLA.US)$ set to release their results. $General Motors (GM.US)$ is scheduled to report earnings on Tuesday. After warning that changes in US policy may affect profits, the company may elaborate on its manufacturing business adjustment plans. $Netflix (NFLX.US)$ is also set to report earnings on Tuesday.
Tesla is scheduled to report earnings on Wednesday, with the company expected to report revenue of $26.58 billion and an estimated EPS of around $0.44, down 29.52% year-over-year.

With the US government shutdown continuing, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) report for September will be released on Friday. Market participants are almost unanimously expecting the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates by another 25 basis points at its meeting on October 28–29, especially given the Fed’s indication that it is about to end its quantitative tightening plan. For the rate cut expectation to change, the upcoming CPI data would need to show inflation pressures far exceeding expectations.

title: Will delist Genting Malaysia
author: Wessex
body: Genting Group proposes a full acquisition offer of 6.74 billion ringgit to delist Genting Malaysia Genting Group (Genting Berhad) will fully acquire its subsidiary Genting Malaysia and plans to delist it from the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange. This is an all-cash conditional acquisition offer with a total transaction value of 6.74 billion ringgit (S$2.1 billion). The move aims to strengthen control over its casino and hotel businesses. According to a Reuters report on Monday (October 13), this acquisition comes as Genting Group seeks to obtain statutory control to strengthen its financial position in preparation for a potential $5.5 billion (S$7.14 billion) casino project in New York State. Genting Group’s U.S. subsidiary is currently participating in the bidding for a gaming license in southern New York State. Genting Group stated that obtaining a majority stake would enable it to better support large-scale investments and streamline capital allocation. Shares of Genting Group and Genting Malaysia were bothsuspended from trading。 Genting Group already holds approximately 49.4% of Genting Malaysia's shares. Its offer price is MYR 2.35 per share, representing a 9.8% premium over Genting Malaysia's closing price of MYR 2.14 last Friday (May 10). The document shows that the acquisition condition is for the group to obtain more than 50% of Genting Malaysia's equity. The group will utilize up to RM6.3 billion in debt financing and internal funds to carry out this acquisition. Genting Group noted that if Genting Malaysia’s public shareholding falls below the regulatory threshold, it does not intend to maintain Genting Malaysia’s listing status; if it successfully secures 90% control of Genting Malaysia, it may delist or compulsorily acquire the remaining shares. The per-share offer price proposed by Genting Group represents a 22.9% premium over Genting Malaysia’s six-month average share price. Based on audited financial data for 2024, the offer implies an enterprise value/EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) ratio of 9.1x, a price-to-earnings multiple of 53x, and a price-to-book ratio of 1.12x. Data from the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) shows that due to weak profitability and cost pressures, Genting Group’s share price has fallen approximately 26% year-to-date, while Genting Malaysia’s share price has declined by 5.3%. Genting Malaysia reported a profit of MYR 251.2 million in 2024. It owns Resorts World Genting in Malaysia and operates casinos in the United States, the United Kingdom, the Bahamas, and Egypt. This acquisition offer is expected to be completed by the end of 2025, subject to approval from the Securities Commission Malaysia.

author: Wessex
body: Analysts: Paving the way for broader restructuring Analysts say the move to privatise GENM could pave the way for a broader restructuring within the Genting group, particularly if it secures the New York licence. Tradeview Capital portfolio manager Neoh Jia Man said the potential privatisation may be designed to facilitate internal reorganisation, including a possible spin-off of GENM’s assets into a real estate investment trust structure to unlock value. He noted that Genting’s shareholders could benefit from the potential award of the new gaming licence in New York state, where GENM remains among the four shortlisted contenders. Neoh told The Business Times: “For minority shareholders, the offer provides an immediate exit at a reasonable premium to current market prices.” He added that while the RM2.35 a share offer appears fair based on trailing price-to-earnings and EV/Ebitda multiples, the roughly 10 per cent premium to GENM’s last-traded price may leave some investors underwhelmed. “That said, there remains room for a potential upward revision to the offer,” he said. Another analyst, who requested anonymity, said the buyout is likely a prelude to more significant corporate manoeuvres in the coming months. “Taking GENM private would give management greater agility to make strategic decisions, particularly if the New York project materialises, which would demand substantial capital investment,” this analyst said. The deal draws comparisons with the 2007 privatisation of Maxis Communications, then Malaysia’s largest mobile operator, by billionaire T. Ananda Krishnan. His RM17.4 billion buyout through Binariang GSM was followed by Saudi Telecom Company’s US$3 billion investment for a 25 per cent stake, which enabled Maxis to expand aggressively in India and Indonesia. “Many minority shareholders at the time felt sidelined,” recalled the analyst. “Once the promoters secured more than half the equity, there was little that the minorities could do to stop the process. Genting’s offer could evoke similar sentiments,” he added.

title: Privatisation of Genting Malaysia (GenM), can be analyzed as follows
author: Wessex
body: The potential for Genting privatisation of Genting Malaysia (GenM), can be analyzed as follows: 1. Elevated Financial Leverage and Credit Rating Pressure Increased Net Gearing: RAM Ratings projects Genting’s net gearing ratio to exceed 0.50 times by 2027, up from current levels, with funds-from-operations (FFO) net debt coverage potentially falling below 0.35 times 2226. This strain could reduce financial flexibility and increase refinancing risks, especially amid rising interest rates. Credit Downgrade Risks: Moody’s warned that Genting’s adjusted debt-to-EBITDA ratio could rise to ~5.1x in 2025 if the GenM acquisition proceeds, exceeding its downgrade threshold of 4.0x 29. A rating downgrade would raise borrowing costs and limit access to favorable financing terms. 2. Liquidity Constraints and Cash Flow Strain Declining Free Cash Flow (FCF): Genting’s FCF fell 40.4% YoY in FY2024 to MYR 2.85B and continued weakening in 2025Q1 (FCF: -MYR 150.47M) 1. Higher debt servicing obligations (e.g., interest payments) could further pressure liquidity, limiting funds for growth initiatives or dividends. Capital Commitments: GenM’s bid for a New York casino license (requiring ~$5.5B in capex) and other projects like Resorts World Las Vegas may demand additional funding, compounding debt risks if privatisation proceeds 2428. 3. Operational Risks from Market Volatility Sector Exposure: Genting’s revenue relies heavily on leisure and hospitality (85.7% in 2024/FY), a sector vulnerable to economic downturns, regulatory changes, and geopolitical disruptions 37. High debt reduces resilience to cyclical downturns. Regional Concentration: Singapore and Malaysia contributed 61.7% of 2024 revenue, exposing Genting to regional economic risks (e.g., tourism fluctuations, currency volatility) 3. 4. Shareholder and Market Sentiment Risks EPS Dilution: Analysts note the GenM privatisation could dilute Genting’s earnings per share due to the premium paid (MYR 2.35/share) and GenM’s underperformance since 2021 2324. Investor Confidence: Market participants question the motives behind privatisation (e.g., avoiding scrutiny of underperforming GenM assets like Empire Resorts) 2830. This could dampen sentiment and trigger stock price volatility. 5. Regulatory and Execution Uncertainties New York License Bid: While GenM’s downstate casino license is viewed favorably, approval delays or higher-than-expected costs could strain finances further 2224. Fiscal Discipline: RAM Ratings highlighted limited debt headroom for major investments post-privatisation, potentially hindering strategic moves 22. Summary Genting’s debt-driven privatisation of GenM introduces risks including heightened leverage, liquidity constraints, operational vulnerabilities, and market skepticism. While the move aims to consolidate control and streamline growth (e.g., New York expansion), the financial strain may outweigh near-term benefits, particularly if macroeconomic or sector-specific headwinds intensify. Investors should monitor credit rating actions, GenM’s license outcomes, and Genting’s ability to stabilize cash flows amid rising obligations.

title: The possibility of Genting Group privatizing Genting Malaysia (GenM) can be analyzed as follows: 🚀🚀🚀🚀🚀
author: Wessex
body: The possibility of Genting Group privatizing Genting Malaysia (GenM) can be analyzed as follows: 1. Rising financial leverage and credit rating pressures Increase in net debt ratio: RAM Ratings forecasts that by 2027, Genting Group's net debt-to-equity ratio will exceed 0.50x, higher than current levels, with Funds from Operations (FFO) net debt coverage potentially dropping below 0.35x. This pressure may reduce financial flexibility and increase refinancing risks, particularly amid rising interest rates. Risk of credit rating downgrade: Moody's warned that if Genting Malaysia’s acquisition proceeds, the group’s adjusted debt-to-EBITDA ratio could rise to approximately 5.1x by 2025, surpassing its downgrade threshold of 4.0x. A downgrade would increase borrowing costs and limit access to favorable financing terms. 2. Liquidity constraints and tight cash flow Decline in Free Cash Flow (FCF): Genting Group’s FCF for the fiscal year 2024 decreased by 40.4% year-on-year to MYR 2.85 billion and continued to weaken in Q1 2025 (FCF: -MYR 150.47 million). Higher debt servicing obligations (e.g., interest payments) may further strain liquidity, limiting funds available for growth initiatives or dividend payouts. Capital commitments: Genting Malaysia’s bid for a New York casino license (requiring approximately USD 5.5 billion in capital expenditure) and other projects like Resorts World Las Vegas may necessitate additional funding. If privatization progresses smoothly between 2024 and 2028, debt risks could intensify further. 3. Operational risks due to market volatility Industry risk: Genting Malaysia’s revenue is heavily reliant on leisure and hospitality (accounting for 85.7% in FY2024), sectors vulnerable to economic downturns, regulatory changes, and geopolitical instability. High leverage reduces resilience against cyclical downturns. Regional concentration: Singapore and Malaysia contributed 61.7% of Genting Group’s revenue in 2024, exposing the group to regional economic risks (e.g., tourism fluctuations, currency volatility). 4. Risks to shareholder and market sentiment Earnings Per Share (EPS) Dilution: Analysts have pointed out that Genting Group’s privatization may dilute its EPS due to the premium paid (MYR 2.35 per share) and the company's underperformance since 2021. Investor Confidence: Market participants have questioned the motives behind the privatization (e.g., avoiding scrutiny of underperforming Genting assets like Empire Resorts). This could dampen market sentiment and trigger stock price volatility. 5. Uncertainty in Regulatory and Enforcement New York License Bid: Despite Genting Malaysia (GenM) being a favored contender for a casino license in southern New York State, delays in approval or higher-than-expected costs could further exacerbate its financial pressures by 2224. Fiscal Discipline: RAM Ratings emphasized that Genting’s limited debt capacity post-privatization for significant investments might hinder its strategic initiatives through 2022. Summary Genting Group’s debt-driven privatization poses risks, including increased leverage, constrained liquidity, operational vulnerabilities, and market skepticism. While the move aims to consolidate control and streamline growth (e.g., expansion into New York), financial pressures may outweigh short-term benefits, especially amid intensifying macroeconomic or industry-specific headwinds. Investors should monitor credit rating actions, the outcome of Genting’s license application, and its ability to stabilize cash flow amid rising debt.

title: GenM privatisation
body:
As the privatisation exercise is ongoing, which may eventually be succeeded, the intrinsic value (fundamental) of Genting shares will soar. This will attract big foreign institutional investor to buy in. The timing of US fed reserve to further cut interest rate at the end of this year, will move big fund rotate to Asia. This is just a sharing of the macro economics insight. Nonetheless, congrats those who buy and hold patiently when the shares at sub rm3.00.
Of I'm not mistaken, while a 90% takeover of GenM allows for a compulsory acquisition, forcing all minority shareholders to sell, a 75% shareholder approval at a general meeting is the standard for a voluntary delisting or a scheme of arrangement. This exercise might took a bit of time, but push factor benefiting Genting is clearly evident.

title: Genting’s Big Move: Will the VTO Fix a Low-Return Giant?
body:
Genting has been in the news recently with its voluntary takeover (VTO) proposal to acquire the remaining 51% of Genting Malaysia Berhad that it does not already own.
In my article written before this announcement, I raised concerns about Genting’s weak ROIC, weighed down by a high fixed-cost base. I viewed Genting more as a defensive cash generator than a true growth compounder. Refer to Genting Berhad: An Asset-Rich but Return-Poor Giant
The VTO signals strategic intent — to unlock better capital allocation, simplify the group structure, and pursue big-ticket ambitions such as potential U.S. expansion.
The move does not change Genting’s underlying operational and efficiency challenges; those remain the key hurdles to long-term value creation.
The weakness lies in capital efficiency — ROIC has rarely cleared 7%. EPS has shrunk over the past decade, and large expansions like Resorts World Las Vegas have lifted fixed costs without delivering matching returns. Unlocking value depends on redeploying cash into higher-return projects and narrowing the gap between ROIC and WACC.
The VTO may simplify Genting’s structure, but only higher returns — not bigger bets — can fix a low-return giant.

title: GENTING BERHAD — MALAYSIA’S SLEEPING GIANT ABOUT TO AWAKEN “When history repeats, fortunes are made.” A GLOBAL CONGLOMERATE READY TO EXPLODE IN VALUE While
author: 心如紫水
body: GENTING BERHAD — MALAYSIA’S SLEEPING GIANT ABOUT TO AWAKEN “When history repeats, fortunes are made.” A GLOBAL CONGLOMERATE READY TO EXPLODE IN VALUE While most investors chase small stories and short-term trades, the real professionals are quietly accumulating one counter — Genting Berhad (3182). For years, Genting Berhad has been deeply undervalued, trading far below its true net asset value (over RM11 per share but if based on latest revaluation, the NTA might reach over RM13.80 per share). But 2026 will not be “just another year.” It will be the turning point, where all of Genting’s global engines fire together — casino, energy, biotech, property, and tourism — pushing it into a new golden era. Make no mistake: Genting Berhad is about to become Bursa Malaysia’s No.1 Super Stock. 1)History Never Lies — The Sentosa Blueprint Repeats Before winning the Sentosa integrated resort license, Genting quietly privatized Genting Singapore, restructured internally, and shocked the world by securing Singapore’s most lucrative casino license. Fast forward to today — Genting Berhad is playing the same winning game plan: Privatize Genting Malaysia, consolidate all U.S. operations, then emerge as the only fully integrated operator ready for New York’s full casino license. History is repeating itself — and every time it does, Genting’s shareholders become the big winners. 2)The New York Jackpot — A License Worth Billions All eyes are now on the New York State Gaming Commission, and every credible source points to one frontrunner: Genting. Genting already operates Resorts World New York City, a proven, tax-paying success story for over a decade. MGM has stepped aside. Wynn has withdrawn. Bally’s faces major financing hurdles. That leaves Genting as the only ready and fully compliant contender with existing infrastructure. Winning this license will instantly transform Genting’s U.S. portfolio into a cash machine — potentially generating over USD 1 billion in annual EBITDA and pushing the group’s valuation to levels unseen in Malaysian corporate history. 3)The Silent Cash Empire — Genting Malaysia While investors debate short-term prices, Genting Malaysia quietly delivers steady profits and robust cash flow from its Resorts World Genting operations. Once privatized, its earnings will fully flow into Genting Berhad — # Stronger consolidated profit # Higher EPS and NTA # Simplified ownership and reduced valuation discount The privatization is not a rumor — it’s a strategic inevitability. Even short sellers know it — having covered back more than 20 million shares recently, reducing their positions from 32.8 million to just 11.6 million. When short sellers retreat, the smart money steps in. 4)Global Expansion — From Las Vegas to London Genting has spent the past few years building quietly but strategically: Expanded ownership in Resorts World Las Vegas, a USD 4.3 billion integrated resort on the Strip. Acquired additional UK casino assets, paving the way for a potential “Genting UK” listing in London. Consolidating Empire Resorts under one brand — creating the foundation for Genting USA, which could one day list on Dow Jones or Nasdaq. Each region — Asia, U.S., U.K. — is now a profit engine waiting for full synergy under Genting’s corporate umbrella. 5)Hidden Value — Billion-Dollar Assets Waiting to Unlock What the market has failed to price in are Genting’s hidden gems: # Miami Waterfront Land: Estimated worth RM4.5–RM5.0 billion, ripe for monetisation. # FLNG (Floating LNG) Project: Poised to contribute sustainable USD revenue starting 2026. # Power Assets: Ready for separate listing — could unlock billions in hidden value. # Taurex Project: Expected government approval in 2026, signaling Genting’s entry into biotech and future energy. Each catalyst alone is massive. Combined — they redefine Genting’s valuation floor. 6)The Balance Sheet Power — Strong, Liquid, and Ready Genting is not a dream story — it’s cash-backed reality. Over RM20 billion in cash and liquid assets. Manageable gearing, diversified revenue in USD, SGD, GBP, and MYR. Continuous positive cash inflow from Malaysia, Singapore, U.S., and U.K. operations. This means Genting doesn’t just survive economic cycles — it thrives in them. 7)Re-Rating Wave Coming — From RM3 to RM9+ At current levels (RM3–RM4), Genting trades at barely one-third of its true intrinsic value. title: Full acquisition of Genting Malaysia poses heavy burden; Fitch may downgrade Genting's rating
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 28th) Due to Genting’s $GENTING (3182.MY)$full acquisition and privatization of Genting Malaysia, $GENM (4715.MY)$this plan has raised concerns from the international rating agency Fitch, as it could increase the financial burden.
According to the latest report, Fitch has placed Genting's long-term Issuer Default Rating (IDR) of 'BBB' on Rating Watch Negative (RWN), indicating that Fitch may downgrade Genting's credit rating in the near future.
In addition to Genting, the bond ratings of its subsidiaries—Genting Malaysia, Genting Overseas Holdings, and Resorts World Las Vegas—have also been placed on negative watch.
Fitch noted that Genting plans to acquire the remaining 50.6% stake in Genting Malaysia for up to MYR 6.7 billion. If a significant number of shareholders accept the offer, this would result in Genting maintaining a high level of leverage over the long term.
"We estimate that Genting's net debt-to-EBITDA ratio could exceed the set sensitivity threshold of 3.5 times after the acquisition, prompting us to consider a downgrade."
Fitch also stated that assuming Genting increases its stake in Genting Malaysia to 60%, the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio would temporarily rise to 3.7 times this year, then gradually decline to 3.4 times in 2026 and 3.1 times in 2027, below the downgrade-triggering threshold of 3.5 times.
"However, if Genting ultimately increases its stake to 66% or higher, the rate of decline in net leverage will slow. In the scenario where Genting holds a larger stake and fully consolidates Genting Malaysia’s earnings, we may adjust Genting's net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to 4.0 times this year, 3.6 times next year, and 3.3 times in 2027."
The agency added that after consolidating earnings, Genting Malaysia is expected to contribute approximately 25% of Genting’s total profits.
New York Gambling License Intensifies Credit Pressure
As Genting's offer price of MYR 2.35 per share represents little premium over Genting Malaysia’s current share price, Fitch stated that it remains uncertain what Genting’s final ownership stake in Genting Malaysia will be.
"Genting may hold a majority stake in Genting Malaysia but may not reach the 75% threshold required for privatization."
Moreover, Fitch pointed out that there is a high likelihood that Resorts World New York, a subsidiary of Genting Malaysia, will secure the new casino license in New York. This could further intensify the credit rating pressures on Genting.
“Genting Malaysia has committed to invest USD 5.5 billion (approximately MYR 23.15 billion), with an initial investment of USD 1.1 billion (approximately MYR 4.63 billion). Currently, we have not incorporated the New York casino license into our baseline forecast.”
The local government of New York will announce the bidding results for the new casino license on December 1.
